source.sourceScope: Whole-paper reading and substantial extraction checkpoint. External proof closure, the normalization repairs, and a final atomization pass remain open; this is not a complete/formalized proof.

summary: Andreatta–Goren–Howard–Madapusi Pera prove the averaged Colmez conjecture (Theorem A) by computing the arithmetic intersection of Borcherds divisors with a big CM cycle on GSpin Shimura varieties (Theorem B), including the ramified and dyadic local deformation calculations, and comparing the metrized Hodge bundles with Faltings heights of CM abelian varieties through the total reflex algebra. Complete (cc-442dc5): every numbered statement is an item, every missing item is routed exactly once, and twenty-seven findings are recorded. Lemma 9.4.4, Proposition 9.4.5 and Lemma 9.4.3 are false as printed (E1–E3), and the corrected BKY12 formula is E26; none affects Theorems A or B. Not formalised. After the review (REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18) there are 212 items (6 library, 16 planned, 190 missing) and 62 source issues. E1–E3 are each false as printed but the paper's later use already matches the corrected versions, so Theorems 9.4.2, 9.5.1 and 9.5.5 and Theorem A hold as printed; the extraction's pending caveats on items 129–134 can be closed. E14 is an error in a stated result: Theorem 4.4.6(3) fails for n = 1 (a discriminant-15 quaternion example has four geometric components at p = 7).

conventions.global: E/F is a CM quadratic extension, [F:Q]=d, with maximal order OE, canonical conjugation c and fixed distinguished complex embedding iota0. Unless explicitly reduced to the classical d=1 case, the orthogonal argument assumes d>1. L is a maximal integral lattice in V=TrF/Q(E,ξ Nm), ξ negative at iota0 and positive at every other real place.
conventions.degree: deg_C(Y)=sum over E-stack Y(C) of 1/|Aut(y)|, not the degree over Z. Y_infinity(C), viewed as a Z-stack, has weighted size 2d deg_C(Y). Arithmetic degrees have finite etale-local lengths log N(q)/|Aut| and one-half of the archimedean sum.
conventions.analytic: L(s,χ) is the finite Hecke L-function. Λ(s,χ)=(D_E/D_F)^(s/2) Γ_R(s+1)^d L(s,χ), Γ_R(s)=π^(−s/2)Γ(s/2). Λ(s)=Λ(1−s). log-derivative at0 is L'/L(0)+1/2 log(D_E/D_F)−d/2 log(4πe^γ).
conventions.local: At nonsplit p of F above rational p, q is the unique E-prime, valuations v_p and v_q give their own uniformizers value1. m=v_p(d_F/Qp), n=v_q(d_E/F)=v_p(D_E/F), f=m+n. Never identify these normalized valuations in the ramified case. Haar measure is self-dual for the chosen additive character; retain both Weil indices when taking nearby ratios.
conventions.badPrimes: a≈_L b means a−b lies in the Q-span of log p for rational p|D_bad,L. This is not equality modulo all bad primes of the enlarged lattice, nor an exact real equality.
conventions.formalization: API and unitTests below are proposed specification tests, not Lean code or assertions that formalization exists. Only explicitly listed scratch computations were executed.

items.name: Integral quadratic lattice carrier and discriminant
items.statement: TauCeti.IntegralLattice (Basic.lean:61) is a full Z-lattice in a Q-vector space with a symmetric Q-bilinear form that is integral on the lattice. Nondegeneracy is the mixin IsNondegenerate (Basic.lean:133). discriminant (Gram.lean:243) is the absolute Gram determinant; for nondegenerate L it equals Nat.card L.DiscriminantGroup, the order of L^∨/L. The paper's maximal lattice L ⊂ (V,Q) is the instance with form [x,y] = Q(x+y) − Q(x) − Q(y). It is nondegenerate and IsEven (Q(L) ⊂ Z), and it is maximal among even lattices. Equivalently, its discriminant quadratic module (L^∨/L, q = Q mod Z) has no nonzero isotropic subgroup, by evenIntermediateCarrierOrderIsoIsotropicSubgroup. D_L = [L^∨ : L] = discriminant. The carrier supplies no maximality predicate and no GSpin datum.
api: Reuse TauCeti.IntegralLattice with explicit IsNondegenerate.
Convert between Q(v) and the bilinear diagonal with a proved factor-of-two convention; reuse discriminant only after that comparison.
unitTests: A degenerate form is allowed by the carrier and must fail the extra nondegeneracy premise.
Changing a unimodular basis preserves the absolute determinant.

items.name: Height-one Breuil–Kisin module
items.statement: Fix a prime p and put W=W(F_p^alg). Let K⊂Frac(W)^alg be a finite extension of Frac(W) (necessarily totally ramified) with uniformizer ϖ, and let E(u)∈W[u] be the Eisenstein polynomial of ϖ with E(0)=p. Let S=W[[u]], with φ: S→S the Frobenius lift extending Fr on W and satisfying φ(u)=u^p. A Breuil–Kisin module over O_K (with respect to ϖ) is a pair (M,φ_M) with M a finite free S-module and φ_M: φ*M[E^{-1}] → M[E^{-1}] an isomorphism of S-modules. The object 1 is S with φ*S=S. M has E-height 1 if φ_M is induced by an S-linear map φ*M→M whose cokernel is killed by E(u).
api: Coefficient-ring construction, Frobenius pullback and linearization; height predicate and base change.
Define integral crystalline specialization u=0, de Rham specialization E=0 and the divided-power comparison as separately typed functors; specify variance.
unitTests: Rank-one linearization E(u) has height1; E(u)^2 does not.
At p=2 use the all-prime classification, not a theorem assuming p>2.
items.note: Existing stage scope, not a library implementation. Import its public interface; this paper supplies the indicated instance and convention checks. Review (REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18): statement corrected against the paper: The paper works over W=W(F_p^alg), an algebraically closed residue field used in §§2.3–2.4 (e.g. the surjectivity in the proof of Prop. 2.4.1), not over W(k) for an arbitrary perfect k. In the paper a Breuil–Kisin module carries only an isomorphism φ_M: φ*M[1/E] ≅ M[1/E]. Integrality of φ_M is the E-height-1 condition, not part of the definition. Kisin's functor produces non-effective modules too, and §3.5 applies it to arbitrary crystalline lattices. Review note: Planned status plausible: FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.4 plans the power-series coefficient ring, Frobenius modules and the Eisenstein height bound.

items.name: All-prime height-one classification
items.locator: §2.1, Theorem 2.1.1 (main assertion), pp. 400–401; proof via [Kis17, Th. 1.1.6] and [Kim12]
items.statement: For every prime p (p=2 by Kim [Kim12]), let M be Kisin's fully faithful tensor functor from Z_p-lattices in crystalline Γ_K-representations to Breuil–Kisin modules over O_K. Then H ↦ M(H) := M(T_p(H)^∨) is an exact contravariant equivalence from the category of p-divisible groups over O_K to the category of Breuil–Kisin modules of E-height 1. (The published first sentence writes M(T_p(H^∨)), which is off by the twist T_p(H^∨)=T_p(H)^∨(1).)
proofOutline: Import R07.4's all-prime classification with hypotheses verified against Kisin/Kim.
Identify the paper's contravariant Dieudonné convention; do not equate Tp(H∨) with Tp(H)^∨ without the cyclotomic twist.
items.note: Existing stage scope, not a library implementation. Import its public interface; this paper supplies the indicated instance and convention checks. Review (REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18): statement corrected against the paper: The item never names the functor. The printed Theorem 2.1.1 says the equivalence is H ↦ M(T_p(H^∨)), yet it then abbreviates M(H) := M(T_p(H)^∨). Since T_p(H^∨) ≅ T_p(H)^∨(1), these differ by a Tate twist, and only M(T_p(H)^∨) lands in E-height 1 (see issue E9). The statement also needs Kisin's functor M on crystalline lattices, which no item defines (coverage row). Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound in direction. The warning about T_p(H^∨) versus T_p(H)^∨(1) is correct, but the item must state the functor explicitly as M(T_p(H)^∨). R07.4 plans the classification of p-divisible groups, including the dyadic case.

items.name: Integral crystalline specialization
items.statement: (Theorem 2.1.1(1)) The φ-equivariant composite φ*M(H)/uφ*M(H) → M(H)/uM(H)[1/p] ≅ D_cris(T_p(H)^∨) ≅ D(H)(W)[1/p] has first arrow induced by φ_{M(H)} and middle isomorphism (2.1.1). It maps φ*M(H)/uφ*M(H) isomorphically onto D(H)(W), the evaluation on W of the contravariant Dieudonné F-crystal of the reduction of H over F_p^alg.
proofOutline: Read the precise Frobenius pullback in the source and translate to the shared R07 API.
Compare reduction with the Dieudonné crystal, not only after inverting p; G1 remains a variance/source gate.
items.note: Existing stage scope, not a library implementation. Import its public interface; this paper supplies the indicated instance and convention checks. Review (REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18): statement corrected against the paper: Theorem 2.1.1(1) says nothing about 'preserving tensors and duality'. It concerns φ*M(H)/u (not M(H)/u), mapped through φ_{M(H)}. The item's 'appropriate u=0 Frobenius specialization' should say exactly this. Review note: Planned at R07.2/R07.4 is plausible. R07.4's description names only a 'generic-fibre comparison', so the integral comparisons of Theorem 2.1.1(1)–(3) (Kis17 1.1.6) should be requested from that layer explicitly.

items.name: Integral de Rham specialization and filtration
items.statement: (Theorem 2.1.1(2)) The filtered isomorphism φ*M(H)/E(u)φ*M(H)[1/p] ≅ K⊗_{Frac(W)}D_cris(T_p(H)^∨) ≅ D(H)(O_K)[1/p] of (2.1.2) maps φ*M(H)/E(u)φ*M(H) isomorphically onto D(H)(O_K). The source filtration is induced by Fil^1φ*M(H)={x: φ_{M(H)}(x)∈E(u)M(H)}; the target filtration is the Hodge filtration Fil^1D(H)(O_K)=Lie(H)^∨.
proofOutline: Transport the filtration through the integral comparison; check the image/kernel definition before identifying Lie H.
Check exact Hodge sequence under the contravariant convention.
items.note: Existing stage scope, not a library implementation. Import its public interface; this paper supplies the indicated instance and convention checks. Review note: Same remark as bk-crys: the integral comparison should be requested explicitly from R07.4.

items.name: Divided-power comparison
items.statement: The BK module after the specified Frobenius base change to the p-adically completed divided-power envelope S of S→OK identifies with evaluation of D(H) on that thickening, compatibly with Frobenius and the specialization maps.
proofOutline: Use the shared divided-power-envelope and crystal suppliers.
Retain the actual PD base and maps; neither bare Witt vectors nor the existence of divided powers proves this comparison.
items.note: Existing stage scope, not a library implementation. Import its public interface; this paper supplies the indicated instance and convention checks. Review note: Statement matches Theorem 2.1.1(3). S is the p-adic completion of the PD envelope of W[u]→O_K, u↦ϖ, and Fil^1 of S⊗_{φ,S}M is (2.1.3). Neither R07.4 nor R07.6 names this S-evaluation comparison; R07.6 is 'integral deformation and ramification consequences'. The planned status needs a request to R07.4. Review (REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18): status changed from planned (FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.4, FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.6) to missing. Neither R07.4 nor R07.6 names the evaluation of the Breuil–Kisin module on Breuil's S (the PD-envelope comparison of Theorem 2.1.1(3)); it is kept as a source item for those layers. items.name: Lubin–Tate formal OE-module
items.statement: For E/Qp finite, uniformizer π and residue size q_E, choose e(X)∈OE[[X]] with e(X)≡πX mod X² and e(X)≡X^q_E mod π. The resulting one-dimensional commutative formal OE-module G has [π]=e and its π-adic Tate module is free of rank1 over OE.
api: Construct coefficient endomorphisms [a], formal law, π-divisible tower and Tate character.
Change the chosen LT coordinate by an OE-linear isomorphism; expose the unramified embedding decomposition.
unitTests: [a] has derivative a; [π] reduces to Frobenius power.
For E=Qp compare the multiplicative LT example; do not claim canonical coordinates.

Source/proof gates in gaps remain binding. Review note: Missing confirmed: no atlas stage plans height-one Lubin–Tate formal O_E-modules. EndoscopicTransfer ET.6a plans the Lubin–Tate tower for GL_n, and tauceti ClassFieldTheory excludes the Lubin–Tate route. The paper uses a Lubin–Tate polynomial; a Lubin–Tate series is a harmless generalisation.

items.name: Explicit rank-one Lubin–Tate BK module
items.statement: Let E0⊂E be the maximal unramified subfield, d0=[E0:Q_p] and Emb(E0)={Fr^i(ι0): 0≤i<d0}, with ι0 induced by E↪K. Put M=S⊗_{Z_p}O_E=⊕_ι S_ι, where S_ι=W_ι[[u]] and W_ι=W⊗_{ι,O_{E0}}O_E, and identify φ*M=M. Let φ_M be multiplication by β=(β_ι), with β_{ι0}=E_{ι0}(u) (the Eisenstein polynomial of ϖ over W_{ι0} with E_{ι0}(0)=ι0(π_E)) and β_ι=1 for ι≠ι0. Then M is free of rank 1 over S⊗O_E and has E-height 1. M_cris := W⊗_Sφ*M = ⊕_ι W_ι, with Frobenius the image of β under φ⊗1 followed by u↦0; this is 1 on the components ι≠Fr(ι0) and 1⊗π_E on Fr(ι0). M_dR := O_K⊗_Sφ*M = ⊕_ι O_{K,ι} with O_{K,ι}=O_K⊗_{ι,O_{E0}}O_E, and Fil^1M_{ι0}={x: E_{ι0}(ϖ⊗1)x=0}, Fil^1M_ι=0 for ι≠ι0. Rationally, D_cris=Frac(W)⊗_{Q_p}E and Fil^1D_dR=e0·D_{ι0}, where e0 is the idempotent of K_{ι0}=K⊗_{ι0,E0}E cutting out the quotient K_{ι0}→K induced by E↪K.
api: Index components by residue embeddings with explicit Frobenius permutation.
Provide β_iota, filtered specialization and rank calculations; preserve the distinction between E and K.
unitTests: For unramified E the cyclic Frobenius product has exactly one nonunit factor.
Rank over S is [E:Qp], not1 unless E=Qp.

Source/proof gates in gaps remain binding. Review (REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18): statement corrected against the paper: The de Rham filtration is not 'the corresponding distinguished embedding ideal'. By (2.2.4) it is the kernel of multiplication by E_{ι0}(ϖ⊗1) on the ι0-component and 0 on the others; rationally it is e0·D_{ι0}. The crystalline Frobenius (1⊗π_E on the Fr(ι0)-component, 1 elsewhere) is also missing.

items.name: Lubin–Tate realization comparison
items.statement: (Prop. 2.2.1) There is an O_E-equivariant isomorphism of Breuil–Kisin modules M(G) := M(T_{π_E}(G)^∨) ≅ M, with M the module of lt-bk. Hence there are O_E-equivariant isomorphisms D(G)(W) ≅ M_cris of F-crystals over W and D(G)(O_K) ≅ M_dR of filtered O_K-modules.
proofOutline: Compute Frobenius eigencharacters and distinguished Hodge quotient.
Apply fully faithful classification, not equality of generic ranks alone.
items.note: No matching declaration or accepted stage with this full scope found. Coalesce at LubinTateFormalModulesAndQuasiCanonicalLifts. Pending paper proposals do not count as planned stages. Source/proof gates in gaps remain binding. Review (REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18): statement corrected against the paper: Minor. The Breuil–Kisin module is M(G) := M(T_{π_E}(G)^∨), built from the dual Tate module. The proof rests on [RZ96, Lemma 1.22] (the filtered φ-module of the Lubin–Tate character), which no item covers (coverage row).

items.name: Conjugate-semilinear special endomorphisms
items.statement: Let E/Q_p be finite with a non-trivial involution τ and F=E^τ; if E/F is unramified, assume the uniformizer π_E lies in F. Let G be the Lubin–Tate O_E-module of §2.2 and R a p-adically complete O_E-algebra. A special endomorphism of G_R is an f∈End(G_R) with f∘[a]=[τ(a)]∘f for all a∈O_E, and V(G_R) is the O_E-module of these, with O_E acting by post-composition. More generally, for a commutative ring R with non-trivial involution τ and an R-module M, V(M,τ)={f∈End(M): f(am)=τ(a)f(m) for all a∈R}, an R-submodule of End(M) under post-composition.
api: Define the semilinear condition, left OE-action and conjugate symmetry of composition.
Keep integral V, V⊗Qp and crystalline realization separate; include zero and base-change maps.
unitTests: Multiplication by a scalar a changes Q by Nm(a).
An arbitrary OE-linear endomorphism need not be special.
items.note: No matching declaration or accepted stage with this full scope found. Coalesce at LubinTateFormalModulesAndQuasiCanonicalLifts. Pending paper proposals do not count as planned stages. Source/proof gates in gaps remain binding. Review (REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18): statement corrected against the paper: G is not an arbitrary 'O_E-module group': it is the Lubin–Tate O_E-module of §2.2. R is a p-adically complete O_E-algebra, and when E/F is unramified π_E is chosen in F (standing convention of §2.3). The pairing lands in O_E only when End_{O_E}(G_R)=O_E, which needs Spec R connected (see the new Prop. 2.3.1 issue). 'Q(f)=f∘f' is extraction notation. The paper also introduces the general V(M,τ), which §2.5 and §3.6 use.

items.name: Special line and Frobenius fixed points
items.statement: V_cris(G) is an O_E-stable subspace of End(M_cris), free of rank 1 over W⊗O_E, and conjugation by φ0 gives an O_E⊗W-linear isomorphism φ: Fr*V_cris(G)[1/p] ≅ V_cris(G)[1/p]. V(G_1) = V_cris(G)^{φ=1}. Composition defines a τ-Hermitian W⊗O_E-valued form on V_cris(G) restricting to the form of Proposition 2.3.1.
proofOutline: Decompose by unramified embeddings and impose conjugate semilinearity.
Apply the Dieudonné comparison to identify actual endomorphisms with Frobenius invariants.
items.note: No matching declaration or accepted stage with this full scope found. Coalesce at LubinTateFormalModulesAndQuasiCanonicalLifts. Pending paper proposals do not count as planned stages. Source/proof gates in gaps remain binding. Review note: Statement matches Lemma 2.3.2, whose proof the paper omits ('easy lemma'). Part (2) needs full faithfulness of Dieudonné theory over F_p^alg (R07.2), and V(G_1):=V(G_{F_p^alg}) via k_E↪F_p^alg induced by ι0.

items.name: Unramified special Hermitian lattice
items.statement: (Prop. 2.3.3) Let E/F be unramified (so π_E∈F) and d0=2r. Then V(G_1)⊂V_cris(G)=⊕_{i=0}^{d0−1}V_{Fr^i(ι0)} consists exactly of the tuples f=(f_i) with: f_0∈V_{ι0}^{Fr^{d0}=1}=V(O_E,τ); f_i=Fr^i((1⊗π_E)f_0) for 1≤i≤r; and f_i=Fr^i(f_0) for r+1≤i≤2r−1. In particular, f↦f_0 is an isometry (V(G_1),⟨,⟩) ≅ (V(O_E,τ), π_E⟨,⟩) of Hermitian O_E-modules, where for x,y∈V(O_E,τ) the element ⟨x,y⟩∈O_E is defined by x∘y = multiplication by ⟨x,y⟩. So V(G_1) is free of rank 1, and a generator f has ⟨f,f⟩∈π_E·O_F^×.
proofOutline: Solve the cyclic Frobenius equations componentwise.
Compute the square of the resulting semilinear generator; retain the π factor in the nearby lattice.

The exact content is the componentwise description of V(G_1) (printed with a_0 for f_0, E10) and the isometry with (V(O_E,τ), π_E⟨,⟩).

items.name: Ramified special Hermitian lattice
items.statement: (Prop. 2.3.4) Let E/F be ramified. Then τ fixes Emb(E0), V_ι=V(W_ι,τ), and V(G_1)⊂V_cris(G) consists exactly of the tuples f=(f_i) with f_0∈V_{ι0} satisfying (1⊗π_E)Fr^{d0}(f_0)=(1⊗τ(π_E))f_0, and f_i=(1⊗π_E/τ(π_E))·Fr^i(f_0) for 1≤i≤d0−1. In particular, W⊗_{Z_p}V(G_1)→V_cris(G) is an isomorphism. If γ∈W_{ι0}^× satisfies (1⊗π_E)Fr^{d0}(γ)=(1⊗τ(π_E))γ, then f↦γ^{-1}f_0 is an isometry (V(G_1),⟨,⟩) ≅ (V(O_E,τ), γτ(γ)⟨,⟩) of Hermitian O_E-modules; here γτ(γ)∈O_F^×.
proofOutline: Use Frobenius/Lang lifting to solve the unit equation.
Check descent of γτγ and compute the induced quadratic form; never substitute an F-uniformizer for π_E.

Source/proof gates in gaps remain binding. Review (REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18): statement corrected against the paper: 'The ramified nearby Hermitian lattice' is not in the paper; nearby Hermitian spaces are §5.1. The paper asserts the componentwise description, the isomorphism W⊗V(G_1)≅V_cris(G), and the isometry f↦γ^{-1}f_0 for any unit γ solving the Frobenius equation. The existence of γ (Lang's theorem) is implicit. The item writes Fr^d for Fr^{d0}.

items.name: Denominator special quasi-endomorphism torsor
items.statement: For μ∈E/OE, choose μ̃∈E. V_μ(G_R) consists of special quasi-endomorphisms f for which f−[μ̃] is an integral OF-linear endomorphism. This is independent of the representative and, when nonempty, is a torsor under V(G_R).
api: Representative-change equivalence, torsor action, inclusions under reduction and μ=0 comparison.
Use normalized v_E to define r(μ)=−v_E(μ̃)>0 for a nonzero coset.
unitTests: V_0=V; adding an integral representative does not change the set.
The zero coset has no forced positive denominator depth.
items.note: No matching declaration or accepted stage with this full scope found. Coalesce at LubinTateFormalModulesAndQuasiCanonicalLifts. Pending paper proposals do not count as planned stages. Source/proof gates in gaps remain binding. Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. The printed r(µ)=−ord_𝔭(µ̃) (E10) must be −ord_E(µ̃): the proof of Prop. 2.4.1 compares r(µ) with ord_E(1−τ(π_E)/π_E)=ord_E(d_{E/F})−1, and [µ̃]∈π_E^{−r(µ)}End(G_R). The torsor claim for general R is also correct: two elements of V_µ(G_R) differ by an element of V(G_R)[π_E^{-1}]∩End_{O_F}(G_R)=V(G_R). The paper states it only for R=O_K/ϖ, in Prop. 2.4.1(2).

items.name: Ramified denominator cutoff
items.statement: (Prop. 2.4.1) Let E/F be ramified, m=ord_E(d_{E/F}) and r(µ)=−ord_E(µ̃) for µ≠0. (1) If µ=0, then V_µ(G_R)=V(G_R). (2) If µ≠0, then V_µ(G_{O_K/ϖ}) is non-empty iff r(µ)≤m−1, in which case it is a torsor under translation by V(G_{O_K/ϖ}). (3) If p≠2 and µ≠0, then V_µ(G_{O_K/ϖ})=∅, since m=1.
proofOutline: Solve integrality of f−μ̃ on the two embedding components.
Translate the conjugate-difference ideal into the different and prove the strict cutoff; do not include r=n.

It asserts a torsor under translation by V(G_{O_K/ϖ}). Part (1) (µ=0) is omitted.

items.name: One-step special-endomorphism obstruction line
items.statement: Assume K=Frac(W)(ι0(E)) and ϖ=ι0(π_E). For k≥1 put G_k := G_{O_K/ϖ^k} (printed G_{O_K/ϖ^{k+1}}, E10), and V_µ(G_k) := V_µ(G_{O_K/ϖ^k}) for µ∈d_{E/F}^{-1}/O_E. Let M_dR=O_K⊗_Sφ*M (free of rank 1 over O_K⊗O_E, with Fil^1 as in (2.2.4)), V_dR=V(M_dR,τ) and V̆_dR=V_dR⊗_{O_E}d_{E/F}^{-1}. Let Ob~_k=V̆_dR⊗_{O_K⊗O_E,1⊗τ(ι0)}O_K/ϖ^k, free of rank 1 over O_K/ϖ^k, and Ob_k=ϖ^{k−1}Ob~_k, a line over F_p^alg. For each k≥1 there is a canonical map ob_{k+1}: V_µ(G_k)→Ob_{k+1}, sending f to the image of its crystalline realization f_{k+1} on the PD thickening O_K/ϖ^{k+1}→O_K/ϖ^k. (1) f lifts to V_µ(G_{k+1}) iff ob_{k+1}(f)=0. (2) For a∈O_E, a·f∈V_{aµ}(G_k) and ob_{k+1}(a·f)=ι0(τ(a))·ob_{k+1}(f).
api: Thickening transition maps, torsion target, additive and twisted OE-linearity.
Define lift existence as a proposition and prove compatibility with reduction.
unitTests: ob(0)=0 for μ=0.
A nonzero obstruction prevents a lift; a zero obstruction cannot be used beyond the next level without iteration.
items.note: No matching declaration or accepted stage with this full scope found. Coalesce at LubinTateFormalModulesAndQuasiCanonicalLifts. Pending paper proposals do not count as planned stages. Source/proof gates in gaps remain binding. Review (REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18): statement corrected against the paper: The hypotheses and objects are missing: K=Frac(W)(ι0(E)), ϖ=ι0(π_E), µ∈d_{E/F}^{-1}/O_E, V̆_dR, Ob~_k and Ob_k. The index fix should be stated rather than deferred. Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. The index fix G_k=G_{O_K/ϖ^k} is forced by three things: V(G_1)=V(G_{F_p^alg}) in §2.3; the thickening O_K/ϖ^{k+1}→O_K/ϖ^k in the proof of 2.5.1; and Lemma 2.5.4, which lifts from G_1 to G_2 through O_K/ϖ². The same page also misprints V_{dR,k}=V_dR⊗O_K/ϖ^{k+1} for ϖ^k (added to E10). The key external input is Grothendieck–Messing, with Zink's theory for p=2 since G is connected (coverage row).

items.name: Crystalline Hodge criterion for lifting
items.statement: Let e=e_E (=e_K). For k≤e let M_k be the evaluation of D(G) on the PD thickening W[u]/(u^k)→O_K/ϖ^k (kernel generated by p). It is free of rank 1 over W[u]/(u^k)⊗O_E, with φ_k: φ*M_k→M_k (φ(u)=u^p). Put V_k=V(M_k,1⊗τ) and V̆_k=V_k⊗_{O_E}d_{E/F}^{-1}. (1) For k≤e, the reduction map V_k→V_cris(G) induces an isomorphism V_k[1/p]^{φ_k=1} ≅ V(G_1)[1/p] (Dwork's trick). (2) Let k<e and f∈V_µ(G_k), and let f̃_{k+1}∈V̆_{k+1}[1/p] be the φ_{k+1}-invariant element attached to f, i.e. the crystalline realization of f on W[u]/(u^{k+1})→O_K/ϖ^k. Put β_{k+1}=Σ_{i=0}^{k}u^i⊗τ(π_E)^{k−i}∈W[u]/(u^{k+1})⊗_{τ(ι0),O_{E0}}O_E. Then ob_{k+1}(f)=0 iff β_{k+1}·f̃_{k+1,τ(ι0)}∈(1⊗τ(π_E)^{k+1})·V̆_{k+1,τ(ι0)}, equivalently iff f̃_{k+1,τ(ι0)}∈(1⊗τ(π_E)−u⊗1)·V̆_{k+1,τ(ι0)}.
proofOutline: Apply the valid Grothendieck–Messing/Zink deformation theorem to the actual nilpotent thickening.
Use the explicit BK coefficient calculation to evaluate the Hodge quotient; source indexing gate G1 must be resolved.

Source/proof gates in gaps remain binding. Review (REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18): statement corrected against the paper: f̃_{k+1} is used without definition, both here and in the paper's statement. By the proof, it is the element of V̆_{k+1}[1/p] characterised by φ-invariance, namely the evaluation of the crystalline realization of f on the PD thickening W[u]/(u^{k+1})→O_K/ϖ^k. The objects e, M_k, φ_k, V_k and V̆_k must also be stated. The printed proof misnames this thickening (new issue).

items.name: Uniformizer raises exact lift depth
items.statement: If f ∈ V_μ(G_k) does not lift to V_μ(G_{k+1}), then for every a ∈ O_E with ord_E(a) = 1, a·f ∈ V_{aμ}(G_k) lifts to V_{aμ}(G_{k+1}) but not to V_{aμ}(G_{k+2}).
proofOutline: Use twisted linearity of the obstruction and the explicit nonzero first obstruction.
Separate unramified and ramified initial calculations before induction.
items.note: No matching declaration or accepted stage with this full scope found. Coalesce at LubinTateFormalModulesAndQuasiCanonicalLifts. Pending paper proposals do not count as planned stages. Source/proof gates in gaps remain binding. Review note: Statement matches Lemma 2.5.3. The proof (p. 413) has two cases. For k<e it applies Lemma 2.5.2(2) at level k+1, which needs k+1<e. For k≥e it uses that O_K→O_K/ϖ^k is a PD thickening. The case k=e−1 falls under neither argument as written when p=2 (new gap issue). It can be closed by extending Lemma 2.5.2(2) to k=e; for p odd, the second argument already covers it.

items.name: Exact local lifting length
items.statement: Assume K=Frac(W)(ι0(E)), ϖ=ι0(π_E), G_k=G_{O_K/ϖ^k} and µ∈d_{E/F}^{-1}/O_E, and let ord_E: V(G_1)_Q→Z∪{∞} be as defined before Lemma 2.5.4 (with ord_E(0)=∞). (Theorem 2.5.5) For f∈V_µ(G_1) and k≥1, f lifts (necessarily uniquely) to V_µ(G_k) iff ord_E(f)≥k.
proofOutline: Use depth-shift inductively from the exact initial obstruction.
Handle zero separately, and prove existence as well as nonexistence at the next level.
items.note: No matching declaration or accepted stage with this full scope found. Coalesce at LubinTateFormalModulesAndQuasiCanonicalLifts. Pending paper proposals do not count as planned stages. Source/proof gates in gaps remain binding. Review (REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18): statement corrected against the paper: The ord_E normalisation is not 'in depth-shift'. It is the definition just before Lemma 2.5.4: ord_E(a·f)=ord_E(a)+ord_E(f), and an O_E-generator of V(G_1) has ord_E=1 if E/F is unramified and ord_E(d_{E/F}) if ramified. No item defines it (coverage row). The hypotheses K=Frac(W)(ι0(E)), ϖ=ι0(π_E), µ∈d_{E/F}^{-1}/O_E and π_E∈F (unramified case) are also missing. Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound for ord_E(0)=∞, since 0 lifts to every level. The attribution of the normalisation to depth-shift is wrong (see statement_issue). The 'immediate' proof from Lemmas 2.5.3–2.5.4 also needs a fact the paper leaves implicit: every g∈V(G_1)_Q with ord_E(g)≥1 lies in a unique V_{µ'}(G_1), µ'∈d_{E/F}^{-1}/O_E. This follows from Prop. 2.4.1(2) by counting V(G_1)-cosets, and gives f=a·g with ord_E(g)=ord_E(f)−1. For dyadic ramified E the proof inherits the Lemma 2.5.3 gap at k=e−1.

items.name: CM type and reflex norm
items.locator: §3 preamble, p. 415 (reflex norm r(A,µ)); §3.4, p. 420 (CM(E)={Φ⊂Emb(E): Φ⊔Φ̄=Emb(E)}); §9.1, pp. 508–509
items.statement: A CM type Φ of E is a subset of Hom(E,C) choosing exactly one embedding in each conjugate pair. Its reflex field is the fixed field of its stabilizer, and the reflex norm is the torus morphism determined by the cocharacter sum indexed by Φ.
api: Complement/conjugation, Galois transport and 2^d type count.
Reflex stabilizer, descent and norm on characters, compatible with products of CM fields.
unitTests: There are2 types for an imaginary quadratic field.
A type is not required to be primitive or Galois invariant.
items.note: Existing stage scope, not a library implementation. Import its public interface; this paper supplies the indicated instance and convention checks. Review (REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18): §3.1 contains no CM types (it defines the cocharacter µ0); CM(E) is defined in §3.4. The paper's reflex norm is the general one of the §3 preamble: for a cocharacter µ of a Q-torus A with field of definition F, r(A,µ)=Nm_{F/Q}∘Res_{F/Q}(µ). The CM-type reflex norm is its instance for µ_Φ. Review note: Planned at ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocity:CM.0 is plausible (CM types and reflex norms on torus/idele objects). ShimuraVarieties:V5 also constructs CM types and reflex norms.

items.name: CM quotient torus and norm-one torus
items.statement: For a Q-algebra R put T_R=Res_{R/Q}G_m. Let T^1_F=ker(Nm_{F/Q}: T_F→G_m), T=T_E/T^1_F and T_so=ker(Nm_{E/F}: T_E→T_F). θ(x)=x/x̄ defines a surjection T_E→T_so inducing T_E/T_F ≅ T/G_m ≅ T_so, where G_m⊂T is the subtorus T_F/T^1_F, identified with G_m by Nm_{F/Q}. (The diagonal G_m→T is this embedding composed with x↦x^d; its kernel is μ_d.) X^*(T_E)=⊕_{ι∈Emb(E)}Z[ι], X^*(T)={Σa_ι[ι]: a_ι+a_ῑ independent of ι} and X^*(T_so)={Σa_ι[ι]: a_ι+a_ῑ=0}. With a distinguished real embedding ι0 of F and a fixed extension ι0∈Emb(E), the cocharacter µ0∈X_*(T_E) is given by ⟨µ0,[ι]⟩=δ_{ι,ι0}; its field of definition is ι0(E). Then r(T_E,µ0)=id_{T_E}, and r(T,µ0): T_E→T is the quotient map. Dimensions: dim T=d+1 and dim T_so=d.
api: Character/cocharacter presentation and scalar similitude map.
Define maximal compact K0 through the local integral character lattices and expose the reflex reciprocity map.
unitTests: For d=1 recover Res_E/Q Gm.
The norm-one torus has dimension d; the quotient T has dimension d+1.
items.note: No matching declaration or accepted stage with this full scope found. Coalesce at ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocityPartII. Pending paper proposals do not count as planned stages. Source/proof gates in gaps remain binding. Review (REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18): statement corrected against the paper: The item reads 'scalar kernel' at face value. The paper's claim that the diagonal G_m↪T_E induces an embedding G_m↪T is false for d≥2: the kernel is μ_d (new issue). The kernel of T→T_so is the subtorus T_F/T^1_F, identified with G_m by Nm_{F/Q}. The item also omits the character lattices (3.1.1), the cocharacter µ0 (3.1.2) and r(T,µ0). K0 lives in §3.2 and is not maximal compact in general (new issue).

items.name: Non-neat zero-dimensional Shimura stack
items.locator: §3.1, p. 416 (Y_K for neat K, i.e. K∩T(Q) torsion-free, and the stack quotient Y_{K'}/(K/K') in general)
items.statement: For open compact K⊂T(Af), Y_K has complex groupoid T(Q)\({h}×T(Af)/K), retaining stabilizers; its canonical model is finite étale over E with Galois action given by the CM reciprocity map.
api: Double-quotient groupoid, level-change finite maps and rational automorphism weights.
Canonical model with explicit reciprocity normalization and passage to neat covers.
unitTests: At non-neat K keep 1/|Aut| rather than count coarse points.
A smaller neat level yields a finite cover, not equal point counts.
items.note: Existing stage scope, not a library implementation. Import its public interface; this paper supplies the indicated instance and convention checks. Review (REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18): Proposition 3.2.1 has no generic assertion. The generic stack Y_K and its Galois action through r_K(T,µ0): Γ_E→T(A_f)/T(Q)K are constructed in §3.1. Review note: Planned at ShimuraVarieties:V4 is plausible: it constructs finite-level torus models as finite étale schemes via reciprocity. Non-neat stack quotients are not explicit there.

items.name: Étale CM integral model at maximal local level
items.statement: (Prop. 3.2.1) Let K⊂T(A_f) be compact open and p a prime with K_p=K0,p (K0,p as corrected in the §3.2 issue). Let Y_K be the normalization of Spec O_E in Y_K. Then Y_K⊗_{O_E}O_{E,p}, with O_{E,p}=O_E⊗Z_p, is finite étale over O_{E,p}. In particular Y0=Y_{K0} is a finite étale algebraic stack over O_E.
proofOutline: Show the local reciprocity inertia image lies in K0,p.
Descend the finite étale model and stack stabilizers through neat level covers.
items.note: No matching declaration or accepted stage with this full scope found. Coalesce at ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocityPartII. Pending paper proposals do not count as planned stages. Source/proof gates in gaps remain binding. Review (REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18): statement corrected against the paper: The item omits 'In particular Y0 is finite étale over O_E', and it depends on K0,p, whose printed definition is defective (new issue).

items.name: Representation-valued Betti variation
items.statement: A rational representation N of T with K-stable lattice gives the local system N_B on the complex CM stack and its Hodge filtration from the Shimura cocharacter. Tensor products, duals and changes of level are functorial.
api: Associated local system from the canonical torsor, Hodge cocharacter eigenspaces.
Integral Betti lattices and compatible rationalization.
unitTests: Trivial representation gives the constant rank-one local system.
Tensor weights add; arbitrary Levi representations are not silently given flat connections.
items.note: Existing stage scope, not a library implementation. Import its public interface; this paper supplies the indicated instance and convention checks. Review note: Statement fine. The Hodge filtration is split by µ0^{-1} through r(T,µ0)_{v0}: C^×→T(R) (3.3.1), and N_B has fibre tN_Ẑ∩N at [(µ0,t)]. Planned at AutomorphicBundles:B0/B2 is plausible for this generic Betti/Hodge part.

items.name: Representation-valued étale system
items.statement: Fix a prime ℓ. For open K'_ℓ⊂K_ℓ the map Y_{K'_ℓK^ℓ}→Y_K is finite étale over O_E[1/ℓ] (proof of Prop. 3.2.1), so Y_ℓ[1/ℓ]=lim_{K'_ℓ}Y_{K'_ℓK^ℓ}[1/ℓ] is a pro-finite Galois cover of Y_K[1/ℓ] with group K_ℓ. The contraction product N_ℓ ↦ (Y_ℓ[1/ℓ]×N_ℓ)/K_ℓ sends continuous ℓ-adic representations of K_ℓ to lisse ℓ-adic sheaves on Y_K[1/ℓ]. (Prop. 3.3.1) If N is an algebraic Q-representation of T and N_Ẑ⊂N_{A_f} a K-stable Ẑ-lattice, then for each ℓ there is a canonical isomorphism Z_ℓ⊗N_B ≅ N_{Z_ℓ}|_{Y_K(C)} of ℓ-adic local systems.
api: Inverse-system construction and continuous action, comparison transport.
Separate l-adic sheaves on the generic model from extensions across residue characteristic l.
unitTests: The Betti/étale comparison respects the OE-action.
Prime-to-p extension is not the crystalline realization at p.
items.note: Existing stage scope, not a library implementation. Import its public interface; this paper supplies the indicated instance and convention checks. Review (REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18): statement corrected against the paper: The paper builds N_ℓ on the integral model Y_K[ℓ^{-1}], not on the generic Y_K. It works for any continuous ℓ-adic representation of K_ℓ, using that the level-change maps Y_{K'_ℓK^ℓ}→Y_K are finite étale over O_E[1/ℓ]. Prop. 3.4.1 relies on this. The item's unit test even separates these sheaves from their extensions across residue characteristics ≠ℓ. Review note: AutomorphicBundles:B2 covers at most the generic-fibre local system. The extension over Y_K[1/ℓ] rests on torus-integral and is not planned there, so that part is missing.

items.name: Abelian scheme from a polarized CM representation
items.statement: Let Nm: T→G_m be induced by Nm_{E/Q}, and let H be a faithful Q-representation of T with a T-invariant symplectic pairing ψ: H×H→Q(Nm), such that the Hodge structure on H from (3.3.1) has weights (0,−1),(−1,0) and is polarized by ψ. For a K-stable lattice H_Ẑ⊂H_{A_f} on which ψ is Ẑ-valued, H_Hdg is the homology of a polarized abelian scheme over Y_{K,C}, classified by Y_{K,C}→X_{r,m,C} (2r=dim_Q H, m² the discriminant of ψ on H_Ẑ). By canonical models this descends to Y_K→X_{r,m,E}, giving A_{H,Q}→Y_K. (Prop. 3.4.1) A_{H,Q} extends canonically to an abelian scheme A_H→Y_K over the whole integral model, and for every prime ℓ the ℓ-adic Tate module of A_H over Y_K[ℓ^{-1}] is canonically isomorphic to H_{Z_ℓ}.
proofOutline: Use the polarized complex torus and canonical-model descent.
Apply Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich at the asserted integral primes, then descend across a neat cover; do not infer good reduction from CM alone over an arbitrary field.
items.note: No matching declaration or accepted stage with this full scope found. Coalesce at ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocityPartII. Pending paper proposals do not count as planned stages. Source/proof gates in gaps remain binding. Review (REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18): statement corrected against the paper: The item restricts the extension to 'the allowed maximal-level primes'. The paper extends A_{H,Q} to an abelian scheme over the whole integral model Y_K, for every K, by Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich away from each ℓ. Prop. 3.4.1 identifies only the ℓ-adic Tate modules. The Betti identification is by construction, and the de Rham one is Prop. 3.5.5(3) (cm-integral-tensors), not part of 3.4.1. Review note: Missing as a whole, but its inputs have owners: the generic construction by ShimuraVarieties:V5 (Siegel canonical model) and PELModuli:M5 (Siegel moduli), and Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich by NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties:R11.5. Cite them as prerequisites.

items.name: Total reflex CM algebra
items.statement: E# is the finite étale Q-algebra with Hom(E#,Qalg)=CM(E). Complex conjugation acts by Φ↦cΦ, making E# a product of CM fields of total degree2^d. The total reflex norm T→Res_E#/Q Gm is given on the character indexed by Φ by the sum of the E-embedding characters in Φ.
api: Finite Galois-set/étale-algebra equivalence, type-indexed idempotents and character map.
Define total reflex type Φ#={Φ:iota0∈Φ}, of cardinality2^(d−1), and orbit decomposition.
unitTests: For d=1 the total reflex algebra is E.
For a split Galois action on type orbits, E# can be a product, not necessarily a field.
items.note: No matching declaration or accepted stage with this full scope found. Coalesce at ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocityPartII. Pending paper proposals do not count as planned stages. Source/proof gates in gaps remain binding.

items.name: Polarized total-reflex representation
items.statement: Let H#=E#, a T-representation through Nm#: T↪T_{E#}. Fix a non-zero ξ∈E# with ι_Φ(ξ)∈R_{>0}·i for every Φ∈CM(E) with ι0∈Φ. (Prop. 3.4.2) Then (x,y)↦Tr_{E#/Q}(ξxȳ) is a T-equivariant symplectic pairing ψ#: H#×H#→Q(Nm), and the Hodge structure on H# from (3.3.1) has weights (0,−1),(−1,0) and is polarized by ψ#. Hence H# is as in Prop. 3.4.1, and A_{H#} has relative dimension 2^{d−1}.
proofOutline: Compute character weights from containment of iota0 in Φ.
Check alternation, nondegeneracy, positivity and similitude before applying polarized-cm-family.
items.note: No matching declaration or accepted stage with this full scope found. Coalesce at ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocityPartII. Pending paper proposals do not count as planned stages. Source/proof gates in gaps remain binding. Review (REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18): statement corrected against the paper: The exact condition on ξ is missing: ξ∈E#, ξ≠0, with ι_Φ(ξ)∈R_{>0}·i for every Φ∈CM(E) containing ι0 (hence ξ̄=−ξ), and ψ#(x,y)=Tr_{E#/Q}(ξxȳ). The dimension 2^{d−1} is a consequence, not part of Prop. 3.4.2.

items.name: Canonical de Rham realization and Hodge tensors
items.statement: (Prop. 3.5.1) For every E-linear algebraic representation M of E⊗_Q T, the vector bundle M_dR,C on Y_K(C) (descended from the constant bundle on {µ0}×T(A_f)/K) has a canonical and functorial descent M_dR,Q to Y_K. In particular, for every Q-representation N of T, the filtered bundle (N_dR,C, Fil•), with Fil• split by µ0, descends functorially to (N_dR,Q, Fil•) over Y_K. Concretely, M_dR,Q=(P_{T,Q}×M)/T. Here P_{T,Q}→Y_K is the canonical T-torsor of isomorphisms O⊗H≅H_dR,Q preserving tensors {t_β} with stabilizer T; H is as in Prop. 3.4.1, H_dR,Q is the relative first de Rham homology of A_{H,Q}, and the torsor is independent of H.
proofOutline: Use AutomorphicBundles B1/B2 canonical principal bundle and tensor descent.
Embed N as a tensor subquotient of H and prove independence of the choice.
items.note: Existing stage scope, not a library implementation. Import its public interface; this paper supplies the indicated instance and convention checks. Review (REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18): statement corrected against the paper: The item omits the main assertion, which is for E-linear representations M of E⊗_Q T (no filtration). The filtered Q-linear statement is its 'in particular'. Review note: Planned at AutomorphicBundles:B1/B2 is plausible. B1 explicitly plans the absolute-Hodge statements, including Deligne's theorem [DMOS82] used here.

items.name: CM crystalline realization via local reciprocity
items.statement: Let q⊂O_E lie over p, W=W(F_q^alg), O_y the completion of Y_K at y∈Y_K(F_q^alg), and Γ_y=Gal(Frac(W)^alg/Frac(O_y)), a finite-index subgroup of I_q. (Prop. 3.5.2) If N_p is a K_p-stable Z_p-lattice in an algebraic Q_p-representation N of T_{Q_p}, then the Γ_y-representation N_{p,y}[1/p] is crystalline (printed Λ_{p,y}[1/p], E11). (Remark 3.5.3) The homomorphism Γ_y→T(Q_p) defining N_p↦N_{p,y} is Γ_y↪I_q^{ab}≅O_{E,q}^×→T(Q_p), and it factors through the image of E_q^×. Let T_q⊂T_{Q_p} be the image of Res_{E_q/Q_p}G_m and K_q=K_p∩T_q(Q_p) (printed T_{E_q}(Q_p)). This gives a functor from K_q-stable lattices in algebraic Q_p-representations of T_q to Γ_y-representations on finite free Z_p-modules, which recovers N_p↦N_{p,y} on K_p-stable lattices.
proofOutline: Factor local reciprocity through the local CM torus T_q.
Apply the integral LT comparison to tensor constructions; distinguish N_p from the undefined Λ_p notation in the printed statement.
items.note: No matching declaration or accepted stage with this full scope found. Coalesce at ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocityPartII. Pending paper proposals do not count as planned stages. Source/proof gates in gaps remain binding. Review (REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18): statement corrected against the paper: Prop. 3.5.2 has no maximal-level hypothesis: it holds for any K, any prime q|p and any y∈Y_K(F_q^alg). It asserts only that N_{p,y}[1/p] is crystalline. The realizations with their tensors and filtrations come in Cor. 3.5.4 and Prop. 3.5.5. Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound (Λ_{p,y}→N_{p,y}). The proof also needs local reciprocity via Lubin–Tate theory, which no item covers (coverage row).

items.name: Integral CM BK functor
items.statement: (Cor. 3.5.4) Let M be an algebraic Q_p-representation of T_q and M_p⊂M a K_q-stable Z_p-lattice. Then there are an F-crystal M_cris,y over W (meaning a finite free W-module J0 with an isomorphism Fr*J0[1/p]≅J0[1/p]) and a filtered finite free O_y-module M_dR,O_y (filtered by direct summands), such that: (1) both are functorial in M_p; (2) there are canonical isomorphisms B_cris⊗_{Z_p}M_{p,y}≅B_cris⊗_W M_cris,y and B_dR⊗_{Z_p}M_{p,y}≅B_dR⊗_{O_y}M_dR,O_y; (3) if M_{p,y}=T_p(H)^∨ for a p-divisible group H over O_y, then M_cris,y≅D(H)(W) and M_dR,O_y≅D(H)(O_y) as F-crystals and filtered modules respectively, and these carry (2) to the canonical p-adic comparison isomorphisms. Construction: M_cris,y=φ*M(M_{p,y})/u and M_dR,O_y=φ*M(M_{p,y})/E(u), for Kisin's functor M over O_y and a uniformizer π_y.
proofOutline: Realize N_p through the local torus/LT tensor construction.
Prove integral tensor compatibility, not only its rational analogue; resolve G1 variance conventions.
items.note: No matching declaration or accepted stage with this full scope found. Coalesce at ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocityPartII. Pending paper proposals do not count as planned stages. Source/proof gates in gaps remain binding. Review (REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18): statement corrected against the paper: Cor. 3.5.4 concerns K_q-stable lattices M_p in algebraic Q_p-representations of T_q, at any point y∈Y_K(F_q^alg); it is not restricted to K0,p or maximal level. The item omits the comparison isomorphisms (2) and the exact hypothesis of (3), namely M_{p,y}=T_p(H)^∨ for a p-divisible group H over O_y. 'Tensor-compatible' is not asserted.

items.name: Functorial integral CM realizations
items.statement: (Prop. 3.5.5, preamble and (1)) For an algebraic Q-representation N of T and a K-stable lattice N_Ẑ⊂N_{A_f}, there is a canonical filtered vector bundle (N_dR, Fil•N_dR) over Y_K. For each prime q⊂O_E with Y_{K,q} étale over O_{E,q} (e.g. q|p with K_p=K0,p, by Prop. 3.2.1), there is also an F-crystal N_cris over Y_{K,F_q}. Both constructions are functorial in (N,N_Ẑ).
proofOutline: Construct local BK lattices with invariant tensors, then glue the de Rham bundle outside and inside the finite exceptional prime set.
Use the étale descent of the local crystal; unrestricted ramified crystalline globalization remains G2.
items.note: No matching declaration or accepted stage with this full scope found. Coalesce at ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocityPartII. Pending paper proposals do not count as planned stages. Source/proof gates in gaps remain binding. Review (REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18): statement corrected against the paper: 'The étale local-model case' should read 'primes q with Y_{K,q} étale over O_{E,q}'. Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. The proof (p. 426) constructs N_cris only when Y_{K,q} is étale over O_{E,q}, while the statement claims it for every q (new gap issue). The globalization also uses [Kis10, Cor. 1.4.3] (a torsor of tensor-preserving trivializations over Z[1/D]) and Blasius–Wintenberger (coverage rows).

items.name: Generic-fiber restriction of integral CM de Rham realization
items.statement: The restriction of the integral filtered vector bundle N_dR to the generic CM stack Y_K is canonically the rational filtered de Rham bundle N_dR,Q of Proposition3.5.1.
proofOutline: Use Blasius–Wintenberger's compatibility of p-adic and de Rham absolute Hodge tensors.
Identify the same T-torsor over each completed local fraction field before gluing.
items.note: No matching declaration or accepted stage with this full scope found. Coalesce at ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocityPartII. Pending paper proposals do not count as planned stages. Source/proof gates in gaps remain binding.

items.name: Evaluation of the integral CM crystal
items.statement: For y∈Y_K(Fq_alg), evaluation of N_cris on the formal divided-power thickening Spf W(Fq_alg) identifies canonically with N_cris,y constructed by Corollary3.5.4. The extraction only closes the scope where the paper supplies the étale-model construction.
proofOutline: Descend the local BK crystal through the finite unramified coefficient extension.
Check Frobenius and its rational inverse; F-crystal here means the broadened isocrystal-integral lattice convention stated before3.5.4.
items.note: No matching declaration or accepted stage with this full scope found. Coalesce at ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocityPartII. Pending paper proposals do not count as planned stages. Source/proof gates in gaps remain binding. Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. The printed (5) says Spf W(F_q), but the formal PD thickening of an F_q^alg-point is Spf W(F_q^alg) (new misprint issue). The statement is also restricted to primes where N_cris is constructed (Y_{K,q} étale).

items.name: Abelian-scheme comparison of integral CM realizations
items.statement: For N=H from Proposition3.4.1, H_dR is the first relative de Rham homology of A_H, and H_cris is the dual of the Dieudonné F-crystal of its special fiber. The dual is part of the statement and must agree with G1 conventions.
proofOutline: Apply the comparison for the dual Tate module, then dualize to homology.
Identify the Hodge filtration and Frobenius, not only the underlying modules.
items.note: No matching declaration or accepted stage with this full scope found. Coalesce at ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocityPartII. Pending paper proposals do not count as planned stages. Source/proof gates in gaps remain binding. Review note: Statement matches Prop. 3.5.5(3). The crystalline half holds only where N_cris is constructed (Y_{K,q} étale). The dual is consistent with the contravariant D: Cor. 3.5.4(3) with H_{p,y}=T_p(A_H) gives H_cris,y=D(A_H[p^∞])(W)^∨.

items.name: Torus action on every realization
items.statement: For each realization ?=Hdg,dR,l,cris, there is a canonical algebraic-group morphism θ_?(N):T_{Q?}→Aut°(N_?), functorial in N; Q? is Q,E,Q_l,Q_p respectively and Aut° is the group of units of the realization endomorphism algebra in the isogeny category.
proofOutline: Use the CM torus action and canonical realization functors.
Check independence of the K-stable lattice after rationalization and compatibility with each coefficient field.

items.name: Standard conjugate-semilinear torus representation
items.statement: V0 consists of conjugate-semilinear endomorphisms of E: f_a(x)=a c(x). Its E-rank is1, T acts through z/c(z), and Q0(f_a)=Tr_F/Q(a c(a)). L0 is the integral OE lattice. The associated Fil1 line is ω0. Q0 is positive definite over R, so its metric must be checked against the printed negative sign (E4).
api: Semilinear/coordinate equivalence, positive norm, OE lattice and realization functors.
Define the hermitian metric only after the positivity check; do not reuse the negative orthogonal metric verbatim.
unitTests: For E=Q(i), Q0(f_1)>0.
Scaling by a changes the norm by the appropriate embeddings of a c(a).
items.note: No matching declaration or accepted stage with this full scope found. Coalesce at ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocityPartII. Pending paper proposals do not count as planned stages. Source/proof gates in gaps remain binding. Review note: The §3.6 part is verified (pp. 428–429): V0=V(H0,c)≅E via a↦(x↦a·c(x)). T_E acts by conjugation, through T_so (by t/t̄), and V0,Z=V(O_E,c). Q0=Tr_{F/Q}⟨x,x⟩_0 and ω0=Fil^1V_{0,dR} are §9.4 content (p. 513), and Q0 is indeed positive definite: Q0(f_a)=Σ_ι|ι(a)|². The metric sign (E4) is for the §9 reviewer.

items.name: Nonsplit criterion for special realizations
items.statement: Let q⊂O_E lie over p, 𝔭⊂O_F the prime under q, y∈Y_K(F_q^alg) and W=W(F_q^alg). Put H_{0,cris,y}=⊕_{q'|p}H_{0,cris,q'}. Here H_{0,cris,q}=D(G_q)(W) for the Lubin–Tate O_{E,q}-module G_q (uniformizer π_q, taken in F_𝔭 when q/𝔭 is unramified, as §2.3 requires), and H_{0,cris,q'}=W⊗_{Z_p}O_{E,q'} with Frobenius Fr⊗1 for q'≠q. Put V_{0,cris,y}=V(H_{0,cris,y},c)=⊕_{𝔭'|p}V_{0,cris,𝔭'}, where V_{0,cris,𝔭'}=V(H_{0,cris,𝔭'},c) and H_{0,cris,𝔭'}=⊕_{q'|𝔭'}H_{0,cris,q'}. (Prop. 3.6.1) The following are equivalent: (1) 𝔭 is not split in E (printed 'in F', E12); (2) V_{0,cris,𝔭}^{φ=1}≠0; (3) Frac(W)⊗_{Z_p}V_{0,cris,𝔭}^{φ=1}→V_{0,cris,𝔭}[1/p] is an isomorphism; (4) Frac(W)⊗_{Z_p}V_{0,cris,y}^{φ=1}→V_{0,cris,y}[1/p] is an isomorphism.
proofOutline: Compute the local reciprocity/Newton cocharacter on V0.
Use the special-line classification and faithful realization comparison; retain the actual base and nonzero premises.

Give the four equivalent conditions and the explicit crystalline setup of §3.6. Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound; the proof itself treats 'split in E'. The description of H_{0,cris,y} ('from the proof of Proposition 3.5.2', p. 429) is a separate coverage row.

items.name: CM supersingular criterion
items.statement: In the setup of the CM integral model and faithful polarized representation, all the associated abelian-scheme fibers at q are supersingular iff p is nonsplit in E. The Newton cocharacter factors through T as in Lemma3.6.3.
proofOutline: Determine slopes from the local CM cocharacter.
Use faithfulness to obtain the reverse implication, rather than inferring it from one trivial representation.
items.note: No matching declaration or accepted stage with this full scope found. Coalesce at ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocityPartII. The proof (p. 430) cites Prop. 3.4.1 for the Dieudonné isocrystal of A_{H,y}, but the input is Prop. 3.5.5(3): H_cris is the dual of the Dieudonné crystal, and duality does not affect isoclinicity. Add PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18/cm-integral-tensors to dependsOn. On p. 431 '(3.6.1)' means Prop. 3.6.1 (new misprint issue).

items.name: Orthogonal GSpin Shimura datum
items.statement: Let (V,Q) be a quadratic space over Q of signature (n,2) with n ≥ 1, L ⊂ V a maximal lattice and D_L = [L^∨ : L]. G = GSpin(V) is the Q-group with G(R) = {g ∈ C⁺(V_R)^× : g V_R g⁻¹ = V_R}. It fits into 1 → G_m → G → SO(V) → 1 with g•v = gvg⁻¹, and ν : G → G_m is the spinor similitude. G(R) acts through SO(V) on D = {z ∈ V_C : [z,z] = 0, [z, z̄] < 0}/C^× ⊂ P(V_C) (4.1.1). D has two components, interchanged by any γ ∈ G(R) with ν(γ) < 0. (G, D) is a Shimura datum with reflex field Q. A representative z = x + iy (x ⊥ y, Q(x) = Q(y) = −1) gives h_z : S → G_R with h_z(i) = xy. K = G(A_f) ∩ C(L̂)^× (4.1.2) is compact open, and its image in SO(V)(A_f) is the discriminant kernel of L̂. M is the n-dimensional algebraic stack over Q (canonical model) with M(C) = G(Q)\D × G(A_f)/K (4.1.3).
api: Clifford embedding, spinor similitude, map to SO and central Gm.
Domain components, Hodge cocharacter and level stabilizers; retain non-neat quotient stacks.
unitTests: H=C(V) has rational dimension2^(n+2).
Do not use norm-one spinGroup as GSpin.
items.note: No matching declaration or accepted stage with this full scope found. Coalesce at OrthogonalIntegralModelsAndKugaSatake. Pending paper proposals do not count as planned stages. Source/proof gates in gaps remain binding. Review (REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18): statement corrected against the paper: GSpin(V) carries no 'scalar Clifford norm' condition: G(R) = {g ∈ C⁺(V_R)^× : gV_Rg⁻¹ = V_R}, and the spinor similitude ν is then automatic. K = G(A_f) ∩ C(L̂)^× lies in G(A_f); only its image in SO(V)(A_f) is the discriminant kernel. The statement also omits n ≥ 1, the sequence 1 → G_m → G → SO(V) → 1, the explicit domain (4.1.1) and the uniformization (4.1.3). Review note: Shimura data and Hodge type are planned at ShimuraData:D4, and canonical models of Hodge-type data at ShimuraVarieties:V6. The GSpin instance, K and the stack M are not planned, so 'missing' is right for the instance; D4 and V6 are its prerequisites.

items.name: Geometric connectedness of the orthogonal stack
items.statement: For maximal L, if n≥2 or D_L is squarefree, the orthogonal Shimura stack M is geometrically connected.
proofOutline: Calculate the spinor-similitude component quotient.
Use strong approximation with the stated isotropy/dimension hypotheses; neither disjunct may be dropped.
items.note: No matching declaration or accepted stage with this full scope found. Coalesce at OrthogonalIntegralModelsAndKugaSatake. Pending paper proposals do not count as planned stages. Source/proof gates in gaps remain binding. Review note: The disjunction is necessary. For n = 1, take (V,Q) = (B⁰, Nrd) with B the indefinite quaternion algebra of discriminant 15 and L = O_B ∩ B⁰. Then ν(K_3) = (Z_3^×)², ν(K_5) = (Z_5^×)², and M has four geometric components (new issue on Theorem 4.4.5). The printed proof never treats n = 2 with V_Qℓ anisotropic (where ℓ² | D_L). The statement still holds there (new issue).

items.name: Full-Clifford Kuga–Satake abelian scheme
items.locator: §4.1, p. 433 (construction and descent of A → M via [MP16, §3]); §4.2, p. 435 (polarization and the finite unramified map to the Siegel stack)
items.statement: The left GSpin representation H=C(V), its C(L)-lattice and a compatible alternating form give a C(L)-equivariant graded Kuga–Satake abelian scheme A→M. H is its homological realization of rank2^(n+2), hence dim A=2^(n+1), correcting the printed dimension (E8).
api: Even/odd grading, right Clifford action, polarization and Hodge filtration.
Embedding V→End_C(H), not V→H as the special-tensor map.
unitTests: For signature(1,2), full-Clifford H has rank8 and A dimension4.
Tensor/right-module conventions must make Clifford multiplication equivariant.
items.note: No matching declaration or accepted stage with this full scope found. Coalesce at OrthogonalIntegralModelsAndKugaSatake. Pending paper proposals do not count as planned stages. Source/proof gates in gaps remain binding. Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. H_B is a variation of type (−1,0),(0,−1) of rank dim_Q C(V) = 2^{n+2} (p. 433), which is the rank of H_1. So the relative dimension is 2^{n+1}, and the printed 'dimension 2^{n+2}' on p. 435 is E8 (confirmed). The Siegel-stack subscript 2^{n+2} recurs on p. 442 as a label only.

items.name: Self-dual smooth integral model at every prime
items.locator: §4.2, Definition 4.2.1 and Theorem 4.2.2 (printed as a Theorem, not a Proposition), p. 435
items.statement: If L_Zp is self-dual, the normalization of the appropriate integral Siegel moduli stack in M yields the smooth integral orthogonal model over Z_(p), with extended Kuga–Satake abelian scheme; this includes p=2 through KMP16.
proofOutline: Import the all-prime Hodge-type integral model theorem.
Verify smoothness and the extension of tensors under self-duality; KMP16 appendix erratum and exact dependency scope remain G2.
items.note: No matching declaration or accepted stage with this full scope found. Coalesce at OrthogonalIntegralModelsAndKugaSatake. Pending paper proposals do not count as planned stages. Source/proof gates in gaps remain binding. Review note: Integral canonical models of Hodge type are not planned in the atlas; ShimuraCompactifications:C5 explicitly excludes all-prime integral canonical models for Hodge type. 'missing' is correct. Proof inputs: [Kis10] for p > 2, [KMP16, Th. 3.10] in general.

items.name: Integral orthogonal de Rham tensors
items.statement: Assume L_(p) is self-dual and let G_(p) = GSpin(L_(p)). The functor (4.2.1) N ↦ N_dR, from algebraic Q-representations of G to filtered vector bundles with integrable connection over M, extends canonically to an exact tensor functor N ↦ N_dR. This extension goes from algebraic Z_(p)-representations N of G_(p) to filtered vector bundles with integrable connection on M_(p). For N = H_(p) it is H_dR, the first relative de Rham homology of A → M_(p). In particular L_(p) gives an embedding V_dR ↪ End_{C(L)}(H_dR) of filtered vector bundles with integrable connection over M_(p). Its image is a local direct summand, and it extends its counterpart (4.1.4) over M.
proofOutline: Use the tensor stabilizer torsor of the integral model.
Check the rank-one isotropic Fil1 and the representation-valued comparison; import generic canonical bundles.
items.note: No matching declaration or accepted stage with this full scope found. Coalesce at OrthogonalIntegralModelsAndKugaSatake. Pending paper proposals do not count as planned stages. Source/proof gates in gaps remain binding. Review (REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18): statement corrected against the paper: Omits the main assertion: an exact tensor functor N ↦ N_dR on algebraic Z_(p)-representations of G_(p), extending (4.2.1) and sending H_(p) to the de Rham homology of A. The embedding lands in End_{C(L)}(H_dR) (C(L)-linear endomorphisms) as a local direct summand. The nondegenerate form on V_dR is stated in §4.3 (p. 437), not in Proposition 4.2.4. Review note: Imported from [KMP16, Prop. 3.7].

items.name: Integral orthogonal crystalline tensors
items.statement: Assume L_(p) is self-dual. There is a canonical functor N ↦ N_cris from algebraic Z_(p)-representations of G_(p) to F-crystals over M_(p),F_p, meaning crystals of vector bundles N with an isomorphism Fr*N ≅ N in the Q_p-linear isogeny category. For N = H_(p) it recovers H_cris, the relative first crystalline homology of A. Its evaluation on the formal completion M̂_p of M_(p) along M_(p),F_p is canonically isomorphic to the p-adic completion of N_dR as a vector bundle with integrable connection. In particular there is a canonical F-crystal V_cris over M_(p),F_p whose evaluation on M̂_p is the p-adic completion of V_dR. It has a canonical embedding V_cris ↪ End_{C(L)}(H_cris) onto a local direct summand, compatible with the de Rham embedding.
proofOutline: Use the integral crystalline Tate tensors and BK comparison.
Prove local freeness and all-prime tensor compatibility rather than asserting rational projectors are integral.
items.note: No matching declaration or accepted stage with this full scope found. Coalesce at OrthogonalIntegralModelsAndKugaSatake. Pending paper proposals do not count as planned stages. Source/proof gates in gaps remain binding. Review (REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18): statement corrected against the paper: Omits the functor statement. The 'generic p-adic realization' comparison is not part of Proposition 4.2.5. The embedding lands in End_{C(L)}(H_cris). The crystal lives on M_(p),F_p, with evaluation on the formal completion M̂_p, and an F-crystal here has its Frobenius isomorphism only in the Q_p-linear isogeny category (p. 436). Review note: Imported from [KMP16, Prop. 3.9]. The paper does not use the dependency bk-dp here.

items.name: Special endomorphism on the orthogonal model
items.statement: Assume L_(p) is self-dual. The G_(p)-equivariant embedding L_(p) ↪ End_{C(L_(p))}(H_(p)) gives embeddings (4.3.1) V_? ↪ End_{C(L)}(H_?) for ? = B, ℓ, dR, cris, each onto a local direct summand. For a section f of V_?, f∘f = Q(f)·id, where Q(f) is a section of 1_?; this is a quadratic form whose bilinear form is nondegenerate for ? = dR, cris. For an M_(p)-scheme S, x ∈ End_{C(L)}(A_S) is special when three conditions hold. Its ℓ-adic realizations over S[1/ℓ] lie in V_ℓ, its crystalline realization over S_{F_p} lies in V_cris, and its de Rham realization lies in V_dR. V(A_S) denotes the special endomorphisms. For S = Spec O with O a p-adically complete Z_(p)-algebra, x ∈ End_{C(L)}(A_S[p^∞]) is special if its crystalline realization lies in V_cris; these form V(A_S[p^∞]).
api: Specialness predicates for abelian schemes and l-divisible groups, realization maps and base change.
Integral quadratic norm and locally constant values on disconnected bases.
unitTests: Zero is special and Q(0)=0.
Do not silently turn a locally constant norm on a disconnected scheme into one global integer.
items.note: No matching declaration or accepted stage with this full scope found. Coalesce at OrthogonalIntegralModelsAndKugaSatake. Pending paper proposals do not count as planned stages. Source/proof gates in gaps remain binding. Review (REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18): statement corrected against the paper: Omits the de Rham condition and the setting (S an M_(p)-scheme, L_(p) self-dual). The endomorphisms are C(L)-linear. The positivity of Q is Proposition 4.3.7 (item special-positive), not part of Definition 4.3.1. Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. The remark 'componentwise on disconnected bases' is the right reading of E13 (confirmed).

items.name: Orthogonal Hodge lifting criterion
items.statement: Assume L_(p) is self-dual. Let O → Ō be a surjection of p-adically complete Z_(p)-algebras whose kernel admits nilpotent divided powers. Let y : Spec O → M_(p) have restriction ȳ to Spec Ō. Let V_O ⊂ End(H_O) be the realization of V_dR on Spec O, with Hodge line Fil¹V_O (projective of rank 1). For x ∈ V(A_ȳ[p^∞]) with crystalline realization x_cris ∈ V_O, x lifts to an element of V(A_y[p^∞]) if and only if the functional [x_cris, ·] : Fil¹V_O → O of (4.3.2) is identically 0.
proofOutline: Apply crystalline deformation theory to H and identify the special tensors.
Translate preservation of the Hodge filtration into one quadratic orthogonality equation.
items.note: No matching declaration or accepted stage with this full scope found. Coalesce at OrthogonalIntegralModelsAndKugaSatake. Pending paper proposals do not count as planned stages. Source/proof gates in gaps remain binding. Review (REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18): statement corrected against the paper: The objects are special endomorphisms of the p-divisible group A_ȳ[p^∞], and the conclusion is lifting to V(A_y[p^∞]). The base hypotheses and L_(p) self-dual are not stated. Review note: Grothendieck–Messing and Serre–Tate inputs are planned at AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A4. The special-endomorphism criterion itself is missing.

items.name: Principal special-endomorphism deformation ideal
items.statement: In the formal deformation space of a geometric point on the self-dual orthogonal model, the locus where a fixed special endomorphism lifts is cut out by a single equation, obtained from its pairing with the universal Hodge line.
proofOutline: Trivialize the Hodge line locally and use special-deformation.
Distinguish 'one equation' from Cartier/non-zero-divisor conclusions, which require separate flatness arguments.
items.note: No matching declaration or accepted stage with this full scope found. Coalesce at OrthogonalIntegralModelsAndKugaSatake. Pending paper proposals do not count as planned stages. Source/proof gates in gaps remain binding.

items.name: Fiberwise specialness and rigidity
items.statement: For a connected M_(p)-scheme S and a C(L)-equivariant x ∈ End(A_S), the following are equivalent: x is special; the fibre of x at every geometric point is special; the fibre of x at some geometric point is special.
proofOutline: Use horizontal sections and Frobenius to compare nearby realizations.
Separate connectedness, reducedness and crystalline base hypotheses; exact three-way statement atomization remains G7.
items.note: No matching declaration or accepted stage with this full scope found. Coalesce at OrthogonalIntegralModelsAndKugaSatake. Pending paper proposals do not count as planned stages. Source/proof gates in gaps remain binding.

items.name: Positive norm of special endomorphisms
items.statement: For an M_(p)-scheme S and x ∈ V(A_S), x∘x = Q(x)·id_{A_S} for an integer Q(x) (locally constant on a disconnected S, see E13), and x ↦ Q(x) is a positive definite quadratic form on V(A_S).
proofOutline: Use the Rosati-positive involution and the Clifford relation.
Use connectedness for constancy, keeping the correction to the unrestricted global-scalar reading.
items.note: No matching declaration or accepted stage with this full scope found. Coalesce at OrthogonalIntegralModelsAndKugaSatake. Pending paper proposals do not count as planned stages. Source/proof gates in gaps remain binding. Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. On S = S1 ⊔ S2, x = (x1, 0) with Q(x1) ≠ 0 gives x∘x = (Q(x1), 0), which is not an integer multiple of id. On connected S the printed statement holds.

items.name: Maximal-lattice model by self-dual enlargement
items.statement: Fix p and an auxiliary maximal lattice L⋄ ⊂ V⋄ of signature (n⋄,2), self-dual over Z_(p), with an isometric embedding (V,Q) ↪ (V⋄,Q⋄) carrying L into L⋄. Let Λ = L^⊥ ⊂ L⋄. M_(p) is the normalization of the smooth model M⋄_(p) in M (Definition 4.2.1). ω is the restriction of Fil¹V⋄_dR to M_(p); it extends Fil¹V_dR. (1) M_(p) and ω do not depend on (V⋄, Q⋄, L⋄). (2) A extends to an abelian scheme A → M_(p), and there is a canonical C(L⋄)-equivariant graded isomorphism A ⊗_{C(L)} C(L⋄) ≅ A⋄|_{M(p)} (4.4.1). (3) There is a canonical isometric embedding Λ ↪ V(A⋄_{M(p)}) (4.4.2). (4) [corrected] Let E/Q_p be finite and t ∈ M(E). If A_t has good reduction over O_E, then t extends to Spec O_E → M_(p). If A_t has only potentially good reduction, t extends over O_{E'} for some finite extension E'/E.
api: Normalization, finite ambient map, auxiliary comparison and descent.
Expose the positive orthogonal complement Λ and its constant special endomorphisms; retain the stack extension-property hypotheses as G2.
unitTests: Two enlargements compare through a common enlargement.
Potential good reduction alone does not assert a section over the original DVR without checking extension/descent.
items.note: No matching declaration or accepted stage with this full scope found. Coalesce at OrthogonalIntegralModelsAndKugaSatake. Pending paper proposals do not count as planned stages. Source/proof gates in gaps remain binding. Review (REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18): statement corrected against the paper: Omits part (3), the canonical isometric embedding Λ ↪ V(A⋄_{M(p)}) (4.4.2), and part (4), the extension property. It also omits that ω is the restriction of Fil¹V⋄_dR. Part (4) as printed is false (new issue): it needs good reduction of A_t over O_E, or it concludes only after a finite extension. Review note: Unit test 2 already anticipates the error in (4), and gap G2 lists it, but no sourceIssue records it; it is recorded here as a new issue.

items.name: Normality and flatness of the special-lattice locus
items.statement: Let p be odd. Let L⋄ be maximal of signature (n⋄,2), self-dual over Z_(p), with L ↪ L⋄ and Λ = L^⊥ of rank at most 2. Let Z(Λ) → M⋄_(p) be the stack of isometric embeddings Λ ↪ V(A⋄_S). If p² ∤ D_L or n ≥ 3, then Z(Λ) is normal and flat over Z_(p), and the map M_(p) → Z(Λ) given by (4.4.2) identifies M_(p) with an open and closed substack of Z(Λ).
proofOutline: Express the deformation equations using the complement's special endomorphisms.
Apply the local-model regularity/normality calculation; do not extrapolate this odd-prime argument to2.
items.note: No matching declaration or accepted stage with this full scope found. Coalesce at OrthogonalIntegralModelsAndKugaSatake. Pending paper proposals do not count as planned stages. Source/proof gates in gaps remain binding. Review (REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18): statement corrected against the paper: The n ≥ 3 branch uses the standing choice that Λ = L^⊥ ⊂ L⋄ has rank at most 2, so that n⋄ ≤ n + 2 (p. 442). The statement omits it, and it should define Z(Λ).

items.name: Local complete intersection of the complement locus
items.statement: For odd p and n≥2, Z(Λ) is a local complete intersection over Z_(p) of relative dimension n, and its special fiber is a local complete intersection over Fp of dimension n, in the auxiliary self-dual setup of§4.4.
proofOutline: Split off one local complement vector after choosing a corank-one complement with discriminant not divisible byp².
Use the single deformation equation on the regular Z(Λ0), and show the special fiber does not contain an irreducible component of Z(Λ0)_Fp.
items.note: No matching declaration or accepted stage with this full scope found. Coalesce at OrthogonalIntegralModelsAndKugaSatake. Pending paper proposals do not count as planned stages. Source/proof gates in gaps remain binding.

items.name: Connected normal special fibers
items.statement: Assume one of the following: (a) L_(p) is self-dual, and n ≥ 2 or D_L is square-free; (b) p is odd, p² ∤ D_L and n ≥ 2; (c) p is odd and n ≥ 5. Then M_(p),F_p (equivalently M_{F_p}) is a geometrically connected and geometrically normal algebraic stack over F_p. When L_(p) is self-dual and n = 1, geometric normality still holds (M_(p) is smooth), but geometric connectedness can fail.
proofOutline: Use connectedness of the generic/ambient model and the local normality argument.
Apply the precise three-branch theorem, not the abbreviated stronger printed consequence.
items.note: No matching declaration or accepted stage with this full scope found. Coalesce at OrthogonalIntegralModelsAndKugaSatake. Pending paper proposals do not count as planned stages. Source/proof gates in gaps remain binding. Review (REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18): statement corrected against the paper: The first branch (L_(p) self-dual) is false for n = 1 when D_L is not square-free. In that case M itself is not geometrically connected, because the hypothesis of Proposition 4.1.1 fails. The item's statement leaves this branch unrestricted. The counterexample is in the new issue on Theorem 4.4.5. Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: unsound. Keeping n ≥ 2 in the second branch is right (E14, confirmed), but the self-dual branch still fails for n = 1. Take V = (B⁰, Nrd) for B the indefinite quaternion algebra of discriminant 15, L = O_B ∩ B⁰ (D_L = 450) and p = 7. Then L_(7) is self-dual, while M, and hence M_(7),F_7, has four geometric components.

items.name: Global normal integral orthogonal stack
items.statement: The local normal maximal-lattice models glue to a unique flat normal algebraic Z-stack M, and the KS abelian scheme extends over M.
proofOutline: Use independence of auxiliary choices on overlaps.
Glue the abelian scheme with its right Clifford action and graded structure.

items.name: Canonical extension of the orthogonal Hodge line
items.statement: The generic line Fil1 V_dR extends canonically to an invertible sheaf ω over the normal integral model M.
proofOutline: Construct the line by the auxiliary self-dual model.
Prove auxiliary independence and gluing; no claim that the full standard V extends as a self-dual bundle at every bad prime.

items.name: Discriminant-coset special quasi-endomorphisms
items.statement: For an M-scheme S, V(A_S) is the group of x ∈ End_{C(L)}(A_S) whose restriction to S_{Z(p)} is special for every p. Here special means that the image under (4.5.1) is special for an auxiliary L⋄ self-dual at p; this does not depend on L⋄ (Proposition 4.5.1). Since K acts trivially on L^∨/L, there is an isometry α_ℓ : Z_ℓ ⊗ (L^∨/L) ≅ V_ℓ^∨/V_ℓ of étale sheaves over M; it extends over M[1/ℓ]. For S over M[1/ℓ] and μ_ℓ ∈ Z_ℓ ⊗ (L^∨/L), V_{μ_ℓ}(A_S[ℓ^∞]) ⊂ V(A_S[ℓ^∞])^∨ is the set of x whose ℓ-adic realization lies in V_ℓ^∨ and maps to α_ℓ(1 ⊗ μ_ℓ) in V_ℓ^∨/V_ℓ. For S over M_(p), choose L⋄ maximal and self-dual over Z_(p) with L ↪ L⋄, and let Λ = L^⊥. View μ_p in Z_p ⊗ Λ^∨/Λ via Z_p ⊗ L^∨/L ≅ Z_p ⊗ L⋄/(L ⊕ Λ) ≅ Z_p ⊗ Λ^∨/Λ. Set V_{μ_p}(A_S[p^∞]) = {x ∈ V(A_S[p^∞])^∨ : ([x], μ_p) lies in the image of (4.5.4)}; this does not depend on L⋄ and agrees with the previous definition over Q (Proposition 4.5.3). For a general S, membership is tested over S_{Z(p)}. Let V(A_S)^∨ = {y ∈ V(A_S)_Q : [V(A_S), y] ⊂ Z}. V_{μ_p}(A_S) is the set of elements of V(A_S)^∨ mapping into V_{μ_p}(A_S[p^∞]). For μ ∈ L^∨/L with p-primary parts μ_p, V_μ(A_S) = ∩_p V_{μ_p}(A_S).
api: Discriminant-group gluing, representative-change equivalence, reduction and orthogonal projection.
Separate V_μ of abelian schemes from the l-divisible local analogues.
unitTests: Changing μ's lift by L preserves the set.
The gluing subgroup L#/(L⊕Λ) need not be the entire product of discriminant groups.

items.name: Special divisor Z(m,μ)
items.statement: For m ∈ Q_{≥0} and μ ∈ L^∨/L, Z(m,μ) → M is the stack over M with Z(m,μ)(S) = {x ∈ V_μ(A_S) : Q(x) = m} for schemes S → M (4.5.7). By (4.5.5) it is empty unless m ≡ Q(μ) mod Z. Since the only special endomorphism x with Q(x) = 0 is 0, Z(0,μ) = ∅ for μ ≠ 0 and Z(0,0) = M.
api: Functor of points, norm fiber, finite morphism and local multiplicity.
Pullback and sum over discriminant gluing classes with the complement's representation sets.

Do not call Z(0,0) a Cartier divisor.

items.name: Cartier and flatness properties of special divisors
items.statement: There is a natural isomorphism Z(m,μ)_Q ≅ Z(m,μ) of stacks over M, with the right-hand side the §4.1 special divisor (4.1.5). (1) If m > 0, then étale locally on the source Z(m,μ) is an effective Cartier divisor on M. (2) If moreover n ≥ 3, Z(m,μ) is flat over Z[1/2]; if in addition L_(2) is self-dual, it is flat over Z.
proofOutline: Use the local single equation and nonzero generic fiber test.
Use integral local models for the non-zero-divisor and flatness assertions.

items.name: Arithmetic divisor and metrized line class
items.statement: An arithmetic divisor on M is a pair Ẑ = (Z, Φ) with Z a Cartier divisor on M and Φ a Green function for Z. That is, Φ is an F_∞-invariant smooth real function on M(C) ∖ Z(C) such that Φ + log|Ψ|² extends smoothly across Z(C) for any local equation Ψ = 0 of Z(C). Principal arithmetic divisors are d̂iv(Ψ) = (div Ψ, −log|Ψ|²) for rational functions Ψ on M, and ĈH¹(M) = Div^(M)/principal (Gillet–Soulé). Metrized line bundles (F_∞-invariant smooth Hermitian metrics) form Pic^(M). The map L̂ ↦ (div Ψ, −log‖Ψ‖²), for any nonzero rational section Ψ, is an isomorphism Pic^(M) ≅ ĈH¹(M) (4.6.1). The tautological bundle ω of Theorem 4.4.6(2) has fibre Cz ⊂ V_C at [(z,g)]. The Petersson metric ‖z‖² = −[z, z̄] makes it ω̂ ∈ Pic^(M).
api: Green-current convention, divisor-to-line equivalence, sums and principal-divisor relations.
Pullback along proper-intersection CM cycles and degree with finite étale-local lengths and half archimedean sum.
unitTests: A principal divisor has zero degree by the product formula.
The negative sign is positive on the orthogonal domain, unlike the positive V0 form in E4.
items.note: Existing stage scope, not a library implementation. Import its public interface; this paper supplies the indicated instance and convention checks. Review (REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18): statement corrected against the paper: Conflates arithmetic divisors with their classes. Div^(M) consists of pairs (Z, Φ) with Z a Cartier divisor and Φ a Green function, and ĈH¹(M) is its quotient by principal arithmetic divisors. The Green-function condition and the isomorphism (4.6.1) Pic^ ≅ ĈH¹ are missing. Review note: Status should be 'missing'. ArakelovGeometryAndAbelianHeights:R35.1 plans Hermitian bundles and arithmetic degree over arithmetic curves only. It does not plan Green functions, Div^ or ĈH¹ of an (n+1)-dimensional arithmetic stack, or (4.6.1). R35.1 supplies only the degree used after pullback to the CM cycle (§6.4). Review (REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18): status changed from planned (ArakelovGeometryAndAbelianHeights:R35.1) to missing. items.name: Integral big CM cycle
items.statement: Assume d > 1, so n = 2d − 2 > 0, and let (V,Q) = (𝒱, Tr_{F/Q}∘𝒬). Let H = C(V) act on itself by left multiplication. Via E♯ ⊂ C⁺(V) (Proposition 5.2.1), T = T_E/T¹_F is the intersection of G and T_{E♯} in GL(H), in a cartesian square with the total reflex norm Nm♯. Res_{F/Q}SO(𝒱) = T¹_E = T_so is a maximal torus of SO(V), V ≅ V_0 as T-representations, and 1 → G_m → T → T_so → 1 maps to 1 → G_m → G → SO(V) → 1. The line z_cm = V(ι0)_C is isotropic and T(C)-stable. T → G gives a morphism of Shimura data (T, {μ0}) → (G, D) sending μ0 to z_cm (5.3.1). Let K_{L,0} = K_0 ∩ K ⊂ T(A_f) and 𝒴 = 𝒴_{K_{L,0}}, the normal integral model over O_E of §3, with generic fibre Y. The induced morphism Y → M (5.3.2) extends to a morphism of Z-stacks 𝒴 → ℳ (Proposition 5.3.1).
api: Map of Shimura data from reflex-clifford, level intersection and integral extension.
Projection to the maximal-level CM model Y0 and comparison of realizations under pullback.
unitTests: Changing level scales both degree and intersection by the same factor.
Count complex points over E; do not multiply the denominator by2d twice.
