It also omits the construction of T ⊂ G (T = G ∩ T_{E♯} in GL(H), cartesian with Nm♯), T_so = Res_{F/Q}SO(𝒱) = T¹_E, z_cm = V(ι0)_C and the morphism of Shimura data (5.3.1). 'Integral extension from the normalization of Spec O_E' misdescribes 𝒴: it is the normal integral model 𝒴_{K_{L,0}} over O_E from §3. The remark on degree and stabilizers is not in §5.3. Review note: The printed proof of Proposition 5.3.1 cites Proposition 3.6.2 (a supersingularity criterion) and Proposition 4.4.1(4), which is false as printed. The correct inputs are Proposition 3.4.1 (A_H is an abelian scheme over 𝒴) and 4.4.1(4) in its good-reduction form; see the new issue.

items.name: CM/orthogonal realization comparison
items.statement: Fix a prime 𝔮 ⊂ O_E over p and an auxiliary maximal lattice L⋄ of signature (n⋄,2), self-dual at p, containing L as an isometric direct summand. It has a smooth model M⋄_(p) over Z_(p) and a finite map M_(p) → M⋄_(p). Let N_(p) be an algebraic Z_(p)-representation of G⋄_(p) = GSpin(L⋄_{Z(p)}), with realizations N⋄_dR over M⋄_(p) and N⋄_cris over M⋄_{F_p} (Propositions 4.2.4, 4.2.5). It also gives a T-representation N = N_(p)[1/p] with the K_{0,L}-stable lattice N_(p) ⊗ Z_p. From these, Proposition 3.5.5 (and its proof) gives N_dR over 𝒴_(𝔮) = 𝒴 ⊗_{O_E} O_{E,(𝔮)} and N_cris over 𝒴_{F_𝔮}. There are canonical isomorphisms N_dR ≅ N⋄_dR|_{𝒴(𝔮)} of filtered vector bundles and N_cris ≅ N⋄_cris|_{𝒴_{F_𝔮}} of F-crystals.
proofOutline: Identify the generic T-representations via Clifford multiplication.
Use the integral BK/crystalline construction at good primes and the auxiliary lattice at the others.

items.name: Good rational prime for a maximal CM lattice
items.statement: For a rational prime p, V_{Q_p} = ⊕_{𝔭|p} V_𝔭 with V_𝔭 = F_𝔭 ⊗_F 𝒱 (printed F_𝔮, a misprint), and L_𝔭 = L_{Z_p} ∩ V_𝔭. The prime p is good for L if two conditions hold. First, for every 𝔭 | p unramified in E (split or inert), L_𝔭 is O_{E,𝔭}-stable and self-dual for the induced Z_p-valued quadratic form. Second, for every 𝔭 | p ramified in E, with 𝔮 the prime of E above 𝔭, L_𝔭 is maximal for the induced Z_p-valued quadratic form, and there is an O_{E,𝔮}-stable lattice Λ_𝔭 ⊂ V_𝔭 with Λ_𝔭 ⊂ L_𝔭 ⊊ 𝔡⁻¹_{E_𝔮/F_𝔭} Λ_𝔭. The other primes are bad, and D_bad = D_{bad,L} is their product. All but finitely many primes are good.
api: Per-F-prime good predicate, global finite bad support and restriction under lattice choices.
Expose the strict ramified upper inclusion for denominator truncation.
unitTests: Equality L_p=d^−1Λ_p is excluded in the ramified branch.

The definitions of V_𝔭 and L_𝔭 = L_{Z_p} ∩ V_𝔭 are missing.

items.name: Incoherent Hilbert Eisenstein series
items.statement: Let ψ_F = ψ_Q∘Tr_{F/Q}. For each archimedean v let C_v be the positive definite rank-2 quadratic space over F_v, C_∞ = ∏_{v|∞} C_v, and C = C_∞ × V̂. Then C is incoherent: it agrees with V ⊗_F A_F at every place except ι0. Let I(s,χ) be the degenerate principal series of SL2(A_F) induced from χ|·|^s, so Φ(n(b)m(a)g,s) = χ(a)|a|^{s+1}Φ(g,s). For φ ∈ S(V̂), with the Gaussian φ^1_∞ = ⊗_{v|∞} e^{−2πQ_v(x)}, the function Φ(g,0) = ω_C(g)(φ^1_∞⊗φ)(0) lies in I(0,χ). It extends to a standard section Φ(g,s), and E(g,s,φ) = Σ_{γ∈B(F)\SL2(F)} Φ(γg,s) (6.1.1) has parallel weight 1 ([KY10, Lemma 4.1]). E(g,s,φ) vanishes identically at s = 0 ([Kud97, Th. 2.2]). With A_F given the ψ_F-self-dual measure and W_α(g,s,Φ) = ∫_{A_F} Φ(wn(b)g,s)ψ_F(−αb)db (6.1.2), the Fourier coefficients are E_α = W_α for α ≠ 0 and E_0 = Φ(g,s) + W_0(g,s,Φ) (6.1.3). W_α factors as W_{α,∞}·∏_𝔭 W_{α,𝔭} for factorisable φ.
api: Schwartz-to-section map, factorized Whittaker integrals, analytic continuation and derivative.
Import generic metaplectic/Weil and Eisenstein machinery; export the specified incoherent CM instance.

items.statement: For α ∈ F^×, Diff(α) = {places v of F : C_v does not represent α}. If α is totally positive, then Diff(α) = {primes 𝔭 ⊂ O_F : V_𝔭 does not represent α} = {𝔭 : χ_𝔭(α) ≠ inv_𝔭(V)}, where inv_𝔭(V) = χ_𝔭(ξ) for V ≅ (E, ξ·Nm).

items.name: Support and logarithmic rationality of positive coefficients
items.locator: §6.2, Proposition 6.2.2, p. 468 (all parts from the statement and proof of [BKY12, Prop. 4.6])
items.statement: Let φ ∈ S(V̂) be arbitrary, and E(τ⃗,s,φ) = N(v⃗)^{−1/2}E(g_τ⃗,s,φ) the classical weight-1 Hilbert Eisenstein series. For every totally positive α ∈ F, N(v⃗)^{−1/2}·E'_α(g_τ⃗,0,φ) = (a_F(α,φ)/Λ(0,χ))·q^α for a constant a_F(α,φ) independent of τ⃗ ∈ H^d. (1) If |Diff(α)| > 1 then a_F(α,φ) = 0. (2) If Diff(α) = {𝔭}, then a_F(α,φ)/Λ(0,χ) ∈ Q(φ)·log N(𝔭), where Q(φ) is the field generated over Q by the values of φ.
proofOutline: Differentiate the local Whittaker product at0.
Use the unique vanishing factor and algebraicity/rationality of the remaining local integrals.

items.name: Corrected constant term of the incoherent derivative
items.locator: §6.2, Proposition 6.2.3, p. 469 (proof pp. 469–471); p. 468 says the corresponding part of [BKY12, Prop. 4.6] is misstated
items.statement: There is a meromorphic M(s,φ) such that N(v⃗)^{−1/2}E_0(g_τ⃗,s,φ) = φ(0)N(v⃗)^{s/2} − N(v⃗)^{−s/2}·(Λ(s,χ)/Λ(s+1,χ))·M(s,φ) (6.2.1). If φ = ⊗_𝔭 φ_𝔭 then M(s,φ) = ∏_𝔭 M_𝔭(s,φ_𝔭), with M_𝔭 as in (6.2.3). Each M_𝔭(s,φ_𝔭) is a rational function of N(𝔭)^s with coefficients in Q(φ_𝔭), and all but finitely many equal 1. M(0,φ) = φ(0), and N(v⃗)^{−1/2}E'_0(g_τ⃗,0,φ) = φ(0)·log N(v⃗) + a_F(0,φ)/Λ(0,χ), where a_F(0,φ)/Λ(0,χ) = −2φ(0)Λ'(0,χ)/Λ(0,χ) − M'(0,φ) (6.2.2).
proofOutline: Compute the zero-index intertwining integrals, including annular support and the additive-measure factor.
Use the functional equation and differentiate; retain the M' term omitted by the cited incorrect formula.

items.locator: §6.2, formal q-expansion and (6.2.7), p. 472; the abbreviations a(m,μ), a_F(α,μ) are in §6.3, p. 472
items.statement: The formal q-expansion is E(τ⃗,φ) = a_F(0,φ) + Σ_{α∈F_+} a_F(α,φ)q^α, with a_F from Propositions 6.2.2–6.2.3. Its formal diagonal restriction is E(τ,φ) = Σ_{m∈Q} a(m,φ)q^m, where a(0,φ) = a_F(0,φ) and a(m,φ) = Σ_{α∈F_+, Tr_{F/Q}α = m} a_F(α,φ) for m ≠ 0 (6.2.7), so a(m,φ) = 0 for m < 0. For a maximal lattice L and μ ∈ L^∨/L put a(m,μ) = a(m,φ_μ) and a_F(α,μ) = a_F(α,φ_μ).

items.name: Stack-weighted arithmetic intersection
items.statement: Y is flat of relative dimension 0 over O_E, so every Cartier divisor on Y is supported in nonzero characteristic. A Green function for such a divisor is any F_∞-invariant R-valued function on Y^∞(C), where Y^∞ = Y ×_{Spec Z} Spec C. CĤ^1(Y) is the group of arithmetic divisors (Z,Φ) modulo div^(Ψ) = (div Ψ, −log|Ψ|²), and Pic^(Y) ≅ CĤ^1(Y). For Z effective, deg^(Z,0) = Σ_{𝔮⊂O_E} log N(𝔮)·Σ_{z∈Z(F_𝔮^alg)} length(O_{Z,z})/|Aut(z)|, with O_{Z,z} the étale local ring. deg^(0,Φ) = ½Σ_{y∈Y^∞(C)} Φ(y)/|Aut(y)|. deg^ extends linearly to a homomorphism Pic^(Y) → R, and [·:Y] : Pic^(M) → R is the composite Pic^(M) → Pic^(Y) → R.
api: Finite support, automorphism weights, pullback and projection formula.

items.name: Local Whittaker normalization and nearby cosets
items.statement: Standing hypotheses (§7.1, p. 475; §7.5, p. 491): p is a good prime for L (Definition 5.3.3), 𝔭 ⊂ O_F is a prime above p that is not split in E, and 𝔮 ⊂ O_E is the prime above 𝔭. m(𝔭) = ord_𝔭(d_{F_𝔭/Q_p}), n(𝔭) = ord_𝔭(D_{E_𝔮/F_𝔭}) (nonzero iff 𝔮 is ramified over F), f(𝔭) = m(𝔭)+n(𝔭). If p ≠ 2 then n(𝔭) ∈ {0,1}; if p = 2 then n(𝔭) ∈ {2e(𝔭)+1} ∪ {2i : 0 ≤ i ≤ e(𝔭)}. L_𝔭 = L_p ∩ V_𝔭 contains a maximal O_{E,𝔮}-stable lattice Λ_𝔭, equal to L_𝔭 and self-dual when 𝔭 is inert. Fix a uniformiser π_𝔭, with π_𝔮 = π_𝔭 if 𝔭 is inert and π_𝔭 = Nm(π_𝔮) if 𝔭 is ramified. Inert: (Λ_𝔭,⟨,⟩) ≅ (O_{E,𝔮}, π_𝔭^{−m}x1x̄2) and (^𝔭Λ_𝔭, ^𝔭⟨,⟩) = (O_{E,𝔮}, π_𝔭^{−m+1}x1x̄2). Ramified: (Λ_𝔭,⟨,⟩) ≅ (O_{E,𝔮}, β_+π_𝔭^{−m}x1x̄2) for a unit β_+, and (^𝔭Λ_𝔭, ^𝔭⟨,⟩) = (O_{E,𝔮}, β_−π_𝔭^{−m}x1x̄2), with β_− = δβ_+, δ ∈ 1+π_𝔭^{n−1}O_{F,𝔭} (O_{F,𝔭}^× if n = 1) and χ_𝔭(δ) = −1. So ξ_𝔭 = π_𝔭^{−m} or β_+π_𝔭^{−m}, and ^𝔭ξ_𝔭 = π_𝔭^{−m+1} or β_−π_𝔭^{−m} (7.1.2). Λ_𝔭 = ^𝔭Λ_𝔭 as O_{E,𝔮}-modules, not isometrically (7.1.1). For a coset λ+Λ_𝔭 ⊂ π_𝔮^{−n(𝔭)}Λ_𝔭, ^{(𝔭)}φ_λ is the characteristic function of ^{(𝔭)}λ + ^{(𝔭)}Λ_𝔭 and ^{(𝔭)}Φ^λ_𝔭 ∈ I_𝔭(s,χ) its standard section. W_{α,𝔭}(I,s,^{(𝔭)}Φ^λ_𝔭) = ∫_{F_𝔭} ^{(𝔭)}Φ^λ_𝔭(wn(b),s)ψ_{F_𝔭}(−αb)db, with db self-dual for ψ_{F_𝔭}, and W*_{α,𝔭} = N(𝔭)^{f(𝔭)/2}·γ_𝔭(^{(𝔭)}V)^{−1}·W_{α,𝔭} (the printed definition on p. 476 is inverted; see the new finding on W*). For λ ∉ Λ_𝔭, r(λ) ≥ 1 is least with λ ∈ π_𝔮^{−r(λ)}Λ_𝔭, and s_λ = ^{(𝔭)}Q(^{(𝔭)}λ).

items.name: Inert unramified Whittaker polynomial
items.statement: Standing hypotheses (§7.1, p. 475; §7.5, p. 491): p is a good prime for L (Definition 5.3.3), 𝔭 ⊂ O_F is a prime above p that is not split in E, and 𝔮 ⊂ O_E is the prime above 𝔭. Suppose 𝔭 is inert in E (so λ = 0). (1) If ord_𝔭(α) < −m(𝔭), then W_{α,𝔭}(I,s,^{(𝔭)}Φ^0_𝔭) = 0. (2) If ord_𝔭(α) ≥ −m(𝔭), then W*_{α,𝔭}(I,s,Φ^0_𝔭) = L_𝔭(s+1,χ)^{−1}Σ_{0≤k≤ord_𝔭(α)+m(𝔭)} (−1)^k N(𝔭)^{−ks}, and W_{α,𝔭}(I,s,^𝔭Φ^0_𝔭) = W_{α,𝔭}(I,s,Φ^0_𝔭) − N(𝔭)^{−m(𝔭)/2}(1+N(𝔭)^{−1}) for all s. Equivalently, W*_{α,𝔭}(I,s,^𝔭Φ^0_𝔭) = (1+N(𝔭)^{−1}) − W*_{α,𝔭}(I,s,Φ^0_𝔭). Here γ_𝔭(V) = 1, γ_𝔭(^𝔭V) = −1, and W*_{α,𝔭} = N(𝔭)^{f(𝔭)/2}·γ_𝔭(^{(𝔭)}V)^{−1}·W_{α,𝔭} (the printed definition on p. 476 is inverted; see the new finding on W*).

items.statement: Standing hypotheses (§7.1, p. 475; §7.5, p. 491): p is a good prime for L (Definition 5.3.3), 𝔭 ⊂ O_F is a prime above p that is not split in E, and 𝔮 ⊂ O_E is the prime above 𝔭. Let 𝔭 be ramified in E and λ ∈ π_𝔮^{−n(𝔭)}Λ_𝔭 ∖ Λ_𝔭, with r(λ) ∈ [1, n(𝔭)] least such that λ ∈ π_𝔮^{−r(λ)}Λ_𝔭. (1) If p ≠ 2 (then n(𝔭) = r(λ) = 1): W*_{α,𝔭}(I,s,^{(𝔭)}Φ^λ_𝔭) = 1 if α ≡ ^{(𝔭)}Q(^{(𝔭)}λ) (mod ^{(𝔭)}ξ_𝔭 O_{F,𝔭}), and 0 otherwise. (2) If p = 2 and r(λ) < n(𝔭): α ≡ Q(λ) (mod ξ_𝔭) ⟺ α ≡ ^𝔭Q(^𝔭λ) (mod ^𝔭ξ_𝔭). W_{α,𝔭}(I,s,^{(𝔭)}Φ^λ_𝔭) ≡ 0 unless these hold, and then W*_{α,𝔭}(I,s,^{(𝔭)}Φ^λ_𝔭) = 1 + χ_𝔭(^{(𝔭)}ξ_𝔭α)N(𝔭)^{−(n(𝔭)−r(λ))s}. (3) If p = 2 and r(λ) = n(𝔭): the two congruences are mutually exclusive, and for each of V and ^𝔭V, W*_{α,𝔭}(I,s,^{(𝔭)}Φ^λ_𝔭) = 1 if α ≡ ^{(𝔭)}Q(^{(𝔭)}λ) (mod ^{(𝔭)}ξ_𝔭), and 0 otherwise. Here W*_{α,𝔭} = N(𝔭)^{f(𝔭)/2}·γ_𝔭(^{(𝔭)}V)^{−1}·W_{α,𝔭} (the printed definition on p. 476 is inverted; see the new finding on W*).
proofOutline: Split the integral into valuation annuli and use the Gauss-character support.
The deformation application only uses r≤n−1; do not use an unverified boundary case.

items.locator: §7.1, Lemma 7.1.5 and equation (7.1.4), in the proof of Proposition 7.1.4, p. 479

Let 𝔭 be ramified in E, so χ = χ_𝔭 has conductor n(𝔭) ≥ 1, and let ψ = ψ_{F_𝔭} with self-dual dy. For α ∈ F_𝔭, ∫_{O_{F,𝔭}^×} χ(y)ψ(αy)dy = N(𝔭)^{−f(𝔭)/2}χ(α)ε_𝔭(χ,ψ) if ord_𝔭(α) = −f(𝔭), and 0 otherwise. Consequently, for λ ∉ Λ_𝔭, Φ = ^{(𝔭)}Φ^λ_𝔭, ξ = ^{(𝔭)}ξ_𝔭 and s_λ = ^{(𝔭)}Q(^{(𝔭)}λ): W_{α,𝔭}(I,s,Φ)^{≤1} = ∫_{|b|≤1}Φ(wn(b))ψ(−αb)db = N(𝔭)^{−f(𝔭)/2}γ_𝔭(^{(𝔭)}V) if α ≡ s_λ (mod ξ), and 0 otherwise.

items.name: Zero-index local correction factor
items.statement: The zero-index Whittaker integral is γ_p(V)N(p)^{−(m+n)/2}L_p(s,χ)/L_p(s+1,χ) for the zero lattice coset, and0 for a nonzero coset. Hence the local factor M_p(s,φ_λ) of the constant-term formula is the constant1 or0 respectively; reconcile W* with this raw formula in G3.
proofOutline: Evaluate the intertwining integral at α=0 separately from the nonzero-α limit.
Insert its normalization in constant-fourier; no continuity in α is assumed.

The G3 reconciliation is resolved: with W* = N^{f/2}γ^{−1}W, 7.1.8 reads W*_0 = L(s)/L(s+1), consistent with (6.2.3) and Cor. 7.1.9.

items.name: Local intersection length coefficient
items.locator: Proposition 7.1.10, p. 484 (ℓ via ord_𝔭(ξ_𝔭^{−1}α)) and Proposition 7.3.2, p. 486 (ℓ via ord_𝔭(α)+m(𝔭), with ℓ = 0 unless (^𝔭μ_p + ^𝔭L_p) ∩ ^𝔭V_𝔭 represents α)

items.name: Corrected raw nearby Whittaker derivative ratio
items.statement: Standing hypotheses (§7.1, p. 475; §7.5, p. 491): p is a good prime for L (Definition 5.3.3), 𝔭 ⊂ O_F is a prime above p that is not split in E, and 𝔮 ⊂ O_E is the prime above 𝔭. Let λ+Λ_𝔭 ⊂ π_𝔮^{−n(𝔭)}Λ_𝔭, let α ∈ F^× with Diff(α) = {𝔭}, and X(α,λ) = {x ∈ ^𝔭λ + ^𝔭Λ_𝔭 : ^𝔭Q(x) = α}. (1) If X(α,λ) = ∅, then W'_{α,𝔭}(I,0,Φ^λ_𝔭) = 0. (2) If X(α,λ) ≠ ∅, then W_{α,𝔭}(I,0,^𝔭Φ^λ_𝔭) ≠ 0 and, for the raw Whittaker functions, W'_{α,𝔭}(I,0,Φ^λ_𝔭)/W_{α,𝔭}(I,0,^𝔭Φ^λ_𝔭) = −(ℓ_𝔭(α)/2)·log N(𝔮). Equivalently, W*'_{α,𝔭}(I,0,Φ^λ_𝔭)/W*_{α,𝔭}(I,0,^𝔭Φ^λ_𝔭) = +(ℓ_𝔭(α)/2)·log N(𝔮) for W* = N(𝔭)^{f/2}γ_𝔭(^{(𝔭)}V)^{−1}W, since γ_𝔭(^𝔭V) = −γ_𝔭(V). Here ℓ_𝔭(α) = (ord_𝔭(ξ_𝔭^{−1}α)+1)/2 if 𝔭 is inert and ord_𝔭(ξ_𝔭^{−1}α)+n(𝔭) if 𝔭 is ramified.
proofOutline: Differentiate the inert/ramified normalized polynomials.
Convert both numerator and denominator with their respective Weil indices, then use N(q)=N(p)^2 inert and N(q)=N(p) ramified.
items.note: No matching declaration or accepted stage with this full scope found. Coalesce at GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights. Pending paper proposals do not count as planned stages. The 'pending G3' hedge can go: the sign is now verified in every case (status_comment). Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. Each case checked (q = N(𝔭), X = q^{−s}, a = ord α + m). Ramified, λ = 0: W*(Φ) = 1 − X^{a+n}, W*(^𝔭Φ)(0) = 2, normalised ratio +ℓ/2·log N(𝔮). Inert, λ = 0: a is odd and W*'(Φ)(0) = (1+q^{−1})(a+1)/2·log q. By the corrected nearby identity of 7.1.2(2), W*(^𝔭Φ)(0) = 1+q^{−1}, so the normalised ratio is +ℓ log q = +ℓ/2·log N(𝔮). Ramified, p = 2, 0 < r < n: W* = 1 ± X^{n−r} with ℓ = n−r, same conclusion. When r = n, p ≠ 2, or X = ∅: W' = 0 and ℓ = 0. The raw ratio carries the extra factor γ(V)/γ(^𝔭V) = −1, because inv_𝔭 flips. The final sign of 7.3.2/7.8.1 is confirmed by positivity of deg^.

items.name: Truncated nearby Schwartz function
items.statement: Decompose μ+L_p into cosets λ+Λ_p over F-primes above p, transport each to the nearby lattice, and retain at the distinguished ramified prime only cosets with v_q(λ)>−n. Multiply by unchanged off-prime factors and sum the retained coset characteristic functions to define ^pφ_μ.

Representative independence and support on the nearby adelic Hermitian space.

A disjoint coset union corresponds to a sum of indicator functions, not their tensor product.

items.name: Normalized nearby orbital integral
items.statement: Normalise the Haar measure on T^so(R) = {s ∈ (E⊗R)^× : ss̄ = 1} to total volume 1, fix any Haar measure on T^so(A_f) = {s ∈ Ê^× : ss̄ = 1}, and give T^so(Q)\T^so(A) the quotient measure. For a prime 𝔭 ⊂ O_F non-split in E, ^𝔭φ ∈ S(^𝔭V̂) and α ∈ F̂^×, set O(α,^𝔭φ) = Vol(T^so(Q)\T^so(A))^{−1}·∫_{T^so(A_f)} ^𝔭φ(sx)ds for any x ∈ ^𝔭V̂ with ^𝔭⟨x,x⟩ = α. If no such x exists, O(α,^𝔭φ) = 0. The value does not depend on x or on the Haar measure of T^so(A_f), and for compact open U ⊂ T^so(A_f), Vol(U) = |T^so(Q)∩U|/|T^so(Q)\T^so(A_f)/U|·Vol(T^so(Q)\T^so(A)).
api: Haar measure, orbit transitivity, stabilizer-volume formula and product factorization.
Rationality and compatibility with finite level and coset translation.

items.name: Local KS p-divisible factorization
items.statement: Let 𝔭 ⊂ O_F be non-split in E and 𝔮 the prime above it. Put L_𝔭 = L_p ∩ V_𝔭, H_𝔭 = C(L_𝔭) ⊂ C(L_p) = H_p, and K_{0,L,𝔮} = K_{0,L,p} ∩ image(E_𝔮^×). H_𝔭 is K_{0,L,𝔮}-stable, and h⊗z ↦ hz is a K_{0,L,𝔮}-equivariant isomorphism H_𝔭 ⊗_{C(L_𝔭)} C(L_p) ≅ H_p (7.4.1). For y ∈ Y(F_𝔮^alg), Remark 3.5.3 gives a crystalline Γ_y-representation H_{𝔭,y} with H_{𝔭,y} ⊗_{C(L_𝔭)} C(L_p) ≅ H_{p,y} (7.4.2). With A[p^∞]_𝔭 as in Prop. 7.4.1, V(A[p^∞]_{𝔭,S}) ⊂ End_{C(L_𝔭)}(A[p^∞]_{𝔭,S}) is the set of elements inducing special endomorphisms of A_S[p^∞]. For η ∈ L_𝔭^∨/L_𝔭: fix L ↪ L⋄ maximal of signature (n⋄,2), self-dual at p, and let Λ^𝔭 ⊂ L⋄_p be the orthogonal complement of L_𝔭. Then Λ^𝔭 ↪ V(A⋄[p^∞]_S) canonically, with orthogonal complement V(A[p^∞]_{𝔭,S}). V_η(A[p^∞]_{𝔭,S}) ⊂ V(A[p^∞]_{𝔭,S})^∨ consists of the x for which ([x],η) lies in the image of V(A⋄_S[p^∞]) → V(A[p^∞]_{𝔭,S})^∨/V(A[p^∞]_{𝔭,S}) ⊕ Λ^{𝔭,∨}/Λ^𝔭. Here η is transported by Λ^{𝔭,∨}/Λ^𝔭 ← L⋄_p/(L_𝔭+Λ^𝔭) → L_𝔭^∨/L_𝔭 (7.4.4).
api: Idempotents for F⊗Qp, local OE actions and Serre tensor maps.
Separate actual p-divisible groups, their BK modules and their rational quasi-endomorphism spaces.

items.locator: §7.5, definition of V_μ(G_{𝔮,y}) and Proposition 7.5.1, p. 492 (proof to p. 494)

items.name: CM class functions and Colmez functional
items.statement: CM^0 is the Q-vector space of locally constant functions a : Γ_Q → Q, constant on conjugacy classes, such that a(σ)+a(cσ) is independent of σ. Each a ∈ CM^0 is uniquely a finite C-linear combination Σ_η a(η)η of Artin characters. Every nontrivial η with a(η) ≠ 0 satisfies η(c) = −η(1), hence L(0,η) ≠ 0. Define Z̃(0,a) = −Σ_η a(η)(L'(0,η)/L(0,η) + ½ log f_η), with L the finite Artin L-function and f_η the Artin conductor. a_{(E,Φ)}(σ) = |Φ ∩ σΦ|, and a^0_{(E,Φ)} is its average (9.1.2) over Γ_Q/Stab(Φ), which lies in CM^0 with a^0(σ)+a^0(cσ) = |Φ|.
api: Finite-quotient factorization, class averaging, CM parity and character expansion.
Import generic Artin L-functions/conductors; define hCol(E,Φ)=Ztilde(0,a0).
unitTests: At identity a_(E,Φ)=d and at complex conjugation it is0.
Only locally constant finite-quotient functions have the required finite character expansion; all continuous functions do not.

The item omits both points. Review note: Oddness check: expanding a + a(c·) = const in matrix coefficients gives a(η)(η(c)+Id) = 0 for nontrivial irreducible η. Status missing is correct.

items.name: Stable Faltings height in the AGHMP metric
items.statement: For a g-dimensional abelian variety with everywhere good reduction over Ok, use its determinant invariant differentials and squared archimedean norm |∫A(C) s∧bar s|. Its normalized arithmetic degree is hFalt; it is independent of the field/model/section after finite good-reduction extension. CM heights here use maximal OE.
api: Determinant Hodge line, integral lattice, archimedean volume and normalized degree.
Provide the exact metric adapter to Yuan–Zhang's (2π)^−g-scaled squared norm: h_YZ=h_AGHMP+g log(2π)/2.

Review note: Planned status: the stable Faltings height itself is ArakelovGeometryAndAbelianHeights:R35.3 ('Stable Faltings height'); R35.2 supplies only the Hodge bundle and integration metric. Cite both. The paper's metric is ||s||² = |∫ s∧s̄| with no (i/2)^g or (2π)^{−g} factor. The stated adapter h_YZ = h_AGHMP + (g/2)log(2π) is right: rescaling ||s||² by (2π)^{−g} adds (g/2)log 2π, which makes Theorem A agree with Yuan–Zhang's formula without a 2π term. The R35.2 normalization must be matched to this one. Review (REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18): R35.3 ('Stable Faltings height') added to the planned stages; R35.2 supplies only the Hodge bundle and metric.

items.name: Trace-normalized top de Rham period
items.statement: Let A be an abelian scheme of relative dimension g over O_{E'}. Tr_dR : H^{2g}_dR(A/O_{E'}) → O_{E'} is an isomorphism, so e0 = Tr_dR^{-1}(1) generates. For every embedding σ : E' → C, ∫_{A^σ(C)} η(e0) = (2πi)^g, hence |∫η(e0)| = (2π)^g. For an arbitrary generator e = u·e0 (u ∈ O_{E'}^×), |∫η(e)| = (2π)^g·|σ(u)|.
proofOutline: Read the DMOS comparison and determine homological/cohomological dual conventions.
Use a trace-normalized generator or retain the unit factor and cancel its global contribution by the product formula; do not infer absolute value1 at each embedding.
items.note: No matching declaration or accepted stage with this full scope found. Coalesce at ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocityPartII. Pending paper proposals do not count as planned stages. Source/proof gates in gaps remain binding. Review (REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18): statement corrected against the paper: Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. The G4 caveat can be closed. The DMOS normalization Tr_dR = (2πi)^{−g}∫ is the one the proof states (check: c1^dR(O(1)) on P^1 has trace 1 and integral 2πi). Over Y0, Tr_dR trivializes H^{2g}_dR(A♯/Y0) globally, so the trace-one generator gives ||e_dR|| = (2π)^{−g} at every complex point, with no product formula needed. This is exactly the identity deg(det(H♯_dR)^)/deg_C(Y0) = [E:Q]·2^{d−1}·log 2π = 2^d·d·log 2π used in Theorem 9.4.2 (see coverage).

items.name: Local total-reflex determinant length
items.statement: At a geometric point y over q of E, the claimed determinant section satisfies length(L_y/im s_y)=2^(d−2)v_q(d_F/Q). The expression is integral, including low-degree cases. This target requires the corrected conductor lengths and the local total-reflex module identification; closure remains G4.
proofOutline: Decompose the local total-reflex algebra, compare the two Hodge quotient lattices and compute their difference of lengths.
Use (9.4.10)–(9.4.13) with corrected signs; independently verify the two conductor values before cancellation.

From the corrected Proposition 9.4.5 and a^0_{(E♯_𝔭,Φ♯_𝔭)} = 2^{d_𝔭−2}(1 + d_𝔭^{-1}Ind χ_𝔭): length C(M,Φ♯_𝔭) = e(P/E_q)·2^{d_𝔭−2}·(2ord_q 𝔡_E − ord_q 𝔡_F), as printed in (9.4.12), and length C(N,Υ_ι0) = +e_P·μ_p(a) = e(P/E_q)·ord_q 𝔡_E, the printed final value of (9.4.13). Then (9.4.10)+(9.4.11) give 2^{d−d_𝔭}[2^{d_𝔭−1}ord_q𝔡_E − 2^{d_𝔭−2}(2ord_q𝔡_E − ord_q𝔡_F)] = 2^{d−2}ord_q 𝔡_F. The printed final values are the positive ones, so E1 and E2 do not reach (9.4.9).

items.name: Discriminant degree of the determinant section
items.statement: deg_hat(Δ)/deg_C(Y0)=2^(d−1)log D_F for the metrized determinant section of §9.4, using the corrected positive metric and verified local-length formula.
proofOutline: Sum reflex-local-length against log N(q) and étale stack weights.
Use the discriminant norm formula and the factor2 from E/F; check the section metric has no unaccounted archimedean contribution.

The sum is Σ_q log N(q)·ord_q(𝔡_F)·2^{d−2}·deg_C(Y0), with Σ_q ord_q(𝔡_F) log N(q) = log N_{E/Q}(𝔡_F O_E) = 2 log D_F.

items.name: Faltings-height and standard Hodge-line comparison
items.statement: 2^−dΣΦ hFalt(E,Φ)=1/4·deg_hat(omegahat0)/deg_C(Y0)+1/4 log D_F−d/2 log(2π), in the corrected/verified metric convention. This is a target pending G4, not established by the false arbitrary-generator trace lemma.
proofOutline: Combine reflex-height, the determinant-line identity and reflex-global-degree.
Compute the global determinant metric by the repaired trace comparison and product formula; prove the2π factor instead of copying it.
items.note: No matching declaration or accepted stage with this full scope found. Coalesce at ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocityPartII. Pending paper proposals do not count as planned stages. Source/proof gates in gaps remain binding. Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. Theorem 9.4.2 is true as printed and is not merely 'pending G4'. (i) With the positive metric ||z||²_0 = |[z,z̄]_0| on ω0 (amended E4), the canonical section of L has norm 1 at every point of Y0^∞(C): [x,y]_0 = 2^{1−d}·Tr_{H♯}(x∘y), and for z ∈ ω0 one gets |det(z)(t)/t̄| = |αβ|^{g/2} = ||z||_0^g with zz̄ = αβ on H^{0,−1} and g = 2^{d−1}. The Faltings metric satisfies ||t||² = ||t∧t̄||_vol. Hence det(H♯_dR)^ = Δ̂ + 2^{d−1}ω̂0 − 2Ω̂♯. (ii) The trace-normalized Lemma 9.4.3 gives deg(det(H♯_dR)^)/deg_C(Y0) = 2d·2^{d−1}·log 2π. The printed exponent −dim A would reverse this sign, and the 2π constants in Proposition 9.5.1 would then fail to cancel. (iii) Proposition 9.4.1 holds (item 131). (9.4.4) uses #Y0^∞(C) = 2d·deg_C(Y0).

items.name: Normalized orthogonal/CM Hodge-line comparison
items.statement: At every prime p ∤ D_bad,L and every 𝔭 | p of F, the maximal O_{E,𝔭}-stable quadratic lattice in L_𝔭 is Λ_𝔭 = t_𝔭·L_{0,𝔭}, with t_𝔭 ∈ (E_𝔭)^× and t_𝔭 t̄_𝔭 O_{F,𝔭} = (ξ·𝔡_{F_𝔭/Q_p})^{-1}. By Lemma 7.7.2, ω_{O_y} = t·ω_{0,O_y}, with t acting through the O_E-structure. At y ∈ Y^∞(C) over ι, ||·||²_{ω,y} = |ι(ξ)|·||·||²_{0,y}. Consequently ([ω̂ : Y] − d̂eg_Y(ω̂0))/deg_C(Y) ≈_L −log N_{F/Q}(tt̄) − log|N_{F/Q}ξ| = log D_F.
proofOutline: Compare the generic T-representations and the archimedean |ι(ξ)| metric factor.
At good primes compute the actual maximal OE-lattice and its integral Fil1, rather than asserting Λ_p=ξ d_F^−1 L0,p; then apply the product formula.
items.note: No matching declaration or accepted stage with this full scope found. Coalesce at ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocityPartII. Q(tx) = Tr_{F/Q}(ξ tt̄ xx̄) is Z_p-integral on O_{E,𝔭} iff ξtt̄ ∈ 𝔡_F^{-1}, since the norms span O_{F,𝔭} (1 is a norm). The maximal O_E-stable lattice therefore has ξtt̄𝔡_F a unit: self-dual in the unramified case, and in the ramified case, including wild p = 2, v_𝔭(Nm t) is unrestricted. The finite contribution is −log N_{E/Q}(t) = log|Nξ| + log D_F up to ≈_L. The archimedean contribution is −½·2deg_C(Y)·Σ_ι log|ι(ξ)|. The printed Λ_𝔭 = ξ𝔡^{-1}L_{0,𝔭}, and the printed target ω ≅ ξ𝔡^{-1}⊗ω0, would instead give 2log D_F − 3log|Nξ|.

items.statement: There are auxiliary data (V', Q') = (E, ξ'·Nm_{E/F}) and a maximal lattice L' ⊂ V' with gcd(D_bad,L, D_bad,L') = 1.

items.name: Averaged Colmez identity
items.locator: §1.1, Theorem A, p. 392; §9.5, Theorem 9.5.5, p. 525 (proof p. 526), combined with Proposition 9.3.1, p. 511
items.statement: For every CM field E of degree 2d with maximal totally real subfield F, averaging over all 2^d CM types, with h^Falt normalized by ||s||² = |∫ s∧s̄| (Definition 9.1.4): 2^{−d}Σ_Φ h^Falt_{(E,Φ)} = −½·L'(0,χ)/L(0,χ) − ¼·log|D_E/D_F| − (d/2)·log(2π), where χ = χ_{E/F} and L(s,χ) is without archimedean factors. Equivalently (Theorem 9.5.5 with Proposition 9.3.1), 2^{−d}Σ h^Falt = 2^{−d}Σ h^Col.
proofOutline: Use height-error and auxiliary-good to put the difference in a finite Q-span of rational prime logarithms.

For each prime p, choose an enlargement of signature(2d,2) self-dual at p with positive binary complement, choose a prescribed-support f avoiding its norms, and use good-prime Borcherds vanishing to kill the p coefficient.
Use Q-linear independence of log primes. Do not replace a congruence by the globally exact printed(9.5.5); G3–G6 are the remaining proof gates.

items.name: Codimension of the non-primitive complement locus
items.statement: Let p be odd, and let L⋄, Λ, Z(Λ) and Z^pr(Λ) be as in Proposition 4.4.2 and its proof, with n ≥ 2. Then the complement of Z^pr(Λ)_{F_p} in Z(Λ)_{F_p} has codimension at least n − ⌊n⋄/2⌋.

items.name: Special endomorphisms form a Hermitian O_E-line
items.statement: Let R be a p-adically complete O_E-algebra with Spec R connected. (1) V(G_R)⊂End(G_R) is O_E-stable and, if non-zero, free of rank 1 over O_E. (2) For x1,x2∈V(G_R) there is a unique ⟨x1,x2⟩∈O_E with x1∘x2=[⟨x1,x2⟩]∈End_{O_E}(G_R)=O_E. (3) (x1,x2)↦⟨x1,x2⟩ is Hermitian: ⟨ax1,x2⟩=a⟨x1,x2⟩, ⟨x1,ax2⟩=τ(a)⟨x1,x2⟩ and ⟨x2,x1⟩=τ⟨x1,x2⟩.
proofOutline: The composite of two τ-semilinear endomorphisms is O_E-linear, hence an element of End_{O_E}(G_R) = O_E.

items.name: Parallel sections vanishing at the closed point
items.statement: Let k be perfect of characteristic p and R = W(k)[[u_1,…,u_n]]/(f), local with residue field k. Let D_R be the p-adic completion of the divided power envelope of (f) in W(k)[[u_1,…,u_n]], and φ : D_R → D_R the continuous extension of u_i ↦ u_i^p. Let M be a finite free D_R-module with a topologically nilpotent integrable connection ∇ : M → M ⊗_{W(k)[[u]]} Ω̂¹_{W(k)[[u]]/W(k)}, and an isomorphism φ*M[1/p] → M[1/p] that is parallel for ∇. If m ∈ M^{∇=0} maps to 0 under M → M ⊗_{D_R} W(k) (u_i ↦ 0), then m = 0.
proofOutline: Parallel sections are determined by their value at the closed point via the Taylor expansion.

items.statement: Let L ⊂ L# (signature (n#, 2), maximal) with Λ = L^⊥ and S → M. (1) There is a canonical isometric embedding Λ → V(A#_S) and an isometry V(A_S) ≅ Λ^⊥ ⊂ V(A#_S). (2) For μ ∈ L#^∨/L# and (μ1, μ2) ∈ (μ+L#)/(L⊕Λ), this gives an injection V_μ1(A_S) × (μ2+Λ) → V_μ(A#_S). (3) These injections give a decomposition of V_μ(A#_S) as the disjoint union of V_μ1(A_S) × (μ2+Λ).
proofOutline: Orthogonal decomposition L#⊗Q = (L⊗Q) ⊕ (Λ⊗Q) and the coset bookkeeping of §4.5.

items.name: Special endomorphisms at big CM points by realizations
items.statement: For a Y-scheme S and a prime p, V(A_S[p^∞]) consists of the endomorphisms whose p-adic realizations over S[1/p] land in (5.4.1) and whose crystalline realizations over S_{F_p} land in (5.4.2). In particular V(A_S) consists of those whose ℓ-adic realizations land in (5.4.1) and crystalline ones in (5.4.2).
proofOutline: Restrict Definition 4.3.1 along Y → M using Proposition 5.3.2.

items.name: No special endomorphisms over split primes
items.statement: If the prime p of F below q is split in E (printed 'split in F', see E12), then V(A_y) = V(A_y[p^∞]) = 0 for all y ∈ Y(F_q^alg).
proofOutline: By Proposition 3.6.1 the φ-invariants of the crystalline special space vanish.

The proof uses Proposition 3.6.1, whose split case is 'split in E', and on p. 462 the result is used to conclude that 𝔮 lies over a prime not split in E (E12, confirmed).

items.name: Adelic special endomorphisms are the nearby space
items.statement: For y over a prime nonsplit in E, the Hermitian space V(A_y[∞])_Q is isometric to ^pV ⊗ A_f, with ^pV the nearby Hermitian space of Definition 5.1.2.
proofOutline: Compute the ℓ-adic components from the CM realizations and the p-component from the Lubin–Tate special line; the invariants change exactly at p and ι0.

items.name: Special endomorphisms at supersingular CM points
items.statement: If p is not split in E, q is the prime above it and y ∈ Y(F_q^alg), then A_y is supersingular, V(A_y) ≠ 0, and Ẑ⊗V(A_y) → V(A_y[∞]) is an isometry of quadratic spaces over Ẑ.
proofOutline: Tate's theorem for endomorphisms of abelian varieties over finite fields, applied to special endomorphisms.

items.name: Vanishing at unrepresented α
items.statement: If α ∈ F_p^× is not represented by ^{(p)}V_p, then W_{α,p}(g_p, 0, ^{(p)}Φ^λ_p) = 0.
proofOutline: Local Siegel–Weil: the value at s = 0 is a representation density, zero when α is not represented.

items.name: Annular terms of the Whittaker integral
items.statement: Standing hypotheses (§7.1, p. 475; §7.5, p. 491): p is a good prime for L (Definition 5.3.3), 𝔭 ⊂ O_F is a prime above p that is not split in E, and 𝔮 ⊂ O_E is the prime above 𝔭. Let 𝔭 be ramified in E, λ ∈ π_𝔮^{−n(𝔭)}Λ_𝔭 ∖ Λ_𝔭, Φ = ^{(𝔭)}Φ^λ_𝔭 (so Φ(g) = Φ(g,0)), s_λ = ^{(𝔭)}Q(^{(𝔭)}λ), and U^t = 1+π_𝔭^tO_{F,𝔭} for t ≥ 1. Let c ∈ O_{F,𝔭} with k = ord_𝔭(c) ≥ 1, and d(k,λ) = 2k − (n(𝔭) − r(λ)). Then Φ(n_−(c)) ≠ 0 only if (n(𝔭)−r(λ))/2 < k < n(𝔭) − r(λ)/2, and in that case Φ(n_−(c)) = ψ(c^{−1}s_λ)·Vol(U^{d(k,λ)})^{−1}·∫_{U^{d(k,λ)}} χ(y)ψ(−c^{−1}s_λ y)dy. In particular W_{α,𝔭}(I,s,Φ)^{>1} = 0 if p ≠ 2.
proofOutline: Iwasawa decomposition of n_−(c) and the support of the section Φ.
items.note: No matching declaration or accepted stage with this full scope found. Coalesce at GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights. Pending paper proposals do not count as planned stages. Source/proof gates in gaps remain binding. Also missing the context: 𝔭 ramified in E, λ ∉ Λ_𝔭, Φ = ^{(𝔭)}Φ^λ_𝔭.

items.name: The sign M(α, λ)
items.statement: Standing hypotheses (§7.1, p. 475; §7.5, p. 491): p is a good prime for L (Definition 5.3.3), 𝔭 ⊂ O_F is a prime above p that is not split in E, and 𝔮 ⊂ O_E is the prime above 𝔭. Let 𝔭 be ramified in E and λ ∉ Λ_𝔭 (p = 2 case of Prop. 7.1.4), with k = ord_𝔭(α)+f(𝔭) and d(k,λ) = 2k−(n(𝔭)−r(λ)). Put M(α,λ) = Vol(U^{d(k,λ)})^{−1}∫_{U^{d(k,λ)}} χ(y(y−(1−s_λ^{−1}α)))dy, so that (7.1.6) gives W* = N(𝔭)^{−ks}M(α,λ) or 1 + N(𝔭)^{−ks}M(α,λ) according as α ≢ s_λ or α ≡ s_λ (mod ξ). Then M(α,λ) = 1 if α ≡ s_λ (mod ξ) and ^{(𝔭)}V_𝔭 represents α; −1 if α ≡ s_λ (mod ξ) and ^{(𝔭)}V_𝔭 does not represent α; and 0 if α ≢ s_λ (mod ξ).
proofOutline: Evaluate the character average; the sign is the Hasse invariant of the local Hermitian space.

items.statement: M_p(s, φ_λ) of (6.2.3) is constant: 1 if λ = 0 and 0 otherwise.

items.name: The Lubin–Tate factor of the Kuga–Satake p-divisible group
items.statement: Let 𝔭 be non-split in E, y ∈ Y(F_𝔮^alg), L_𝔭 = L_p ∩ V_𝔭 ⊂ L_p = L⊗Z_p. The Γ_y-module H_{𝔭,y} of (7.4.2) is canonically isomorphic to the p-adic Tate module of a C(L_𝔭)-linear p-divisible subgroup A[p^∞]_𝔭 ⊂ A[p^∞]|_{Spec O_y}, where A is the Kuga–Satake abelian scheme of L. The natural C(L_p)-linear map A[p^∞]_𝔭 ⊗_{C(L_𝔭)} C(L_p) → A[p^∞]|_{Spec O_y} is an isomorphism.
proofOutline: Tate's full faithfulness over O_y applied to the Clifford-module decomposition of the Tate module.

Here 'L#_p' and 'A#' mean the rational-prime lattice L_p = L⊗Z_p and the Kuga–Satake scheme A of L itself. §7.4.1–7.4.3 involve no auxiliary lattice, so a formaliser would misread these items.

items.name: Constant complement of the local special lattice
items.statement: Let L^𝔭_p = L_𝔭^⊥ ⊂ L_p (L_p = L⊗Z_p). There is a canonical isometric embedding L^𝔭_p ↪ V(A[p^∞]_{Spec O_y}) onto a direct summand, where A is the Kuga–Satake scheme of L. For every O_y-scheme S, V(A[p^∞]_{𝔭,S}) = (L^𝔭_p)^⊥ ⊂ V(A_S[p^∞]).
proofOutline: As Lemma 4.5.2, one prime at a time.

items.name: Local coset decomposition
items.statement: For μ_p ∈ L_p^∨/L_p (L_p = L⊗Z_p) and any O_y-scheme S: V_{μ_p}(A_S[p^∞]) = ⊔_{(μ1,μ2)} V_{μ1}(A[p^∞]_{𝔭,S}) × (μ2 + L^𝔭_p), over (μ1,μ2) ∈ (μ_p+L_p)/(L_𝔭 ⊕ L^𝔭_p) ⊂ L_𝔭^∨/L_𝔭 ⊕ L^{𝔭,∨}_p/L^𝔭_p. Here A is the Kuga–Satake scheme of L, not the auxiliary A⋄.

items.name: Crystalline description of the coset subsets
items.statement: V_μ(A_y[p^∞]_p) ⊂ V(A_y[p^∞]_p)_Q consists of the x whose crystalline realization lies in V^∨_{p,cris,y} and satisfies x_cris ≡ η(1⊗μ) mod V_{p,cris,y}.

items.name: Support of the special zero-cycles
items.statement: For α ∈ F_+ and μ ∈ L^∨/L, Z_F(α, μ) is nonempty only if Diff(α) = {p} for a single prime p, and then it is 0-dimensional and supported at the unique prime q of O_E above p.
proofOutline: A point needs a special endomorphism of norm α in ^pV, which exists only when ^pV represents α at every place.

items.name: Coset subsets are the nearby Schwartz function
items.statement: Let 𝔭 ⊂ O_F be non-split in E, lying over a prime p good for L, with 𝔮 the prime above it, and let y ∈ Y(F_𝔮^alg). The A_{f,E}-linear isometry V(A_y[∞])_Q ≅ ^𝔭V̂ of Proposition 5.4.4 can be chosen so that, for every μ ∈ L^∨/L, the characteristic function of the image of V_μ(A_y[∞]) = ∏_ℓ V_{μ_ℓ}(A_y[ℓ^∞]) is the nearby Schwartz function ^𝔭φ_μ of (7.2.3).
proofOutline: Match lattices prime by prime: away from p by the Tate modules, at p by Lemma 7.5.3 and §2.

items.name: The torus acts simply transitively on CM points
items.statement: Let 𝔮 ⊂ O_E lie over a rational prime p good for L. The group T(A_f)/T(Q)K_{L,0} acts simply transitively on the isomorphism classes of Y(F_𝔮^alg), and every y ∈ Y(F_𝔮^alg) has Aut(y) = T(Q) ∩ K_{L,0}. For every t ∈ T(A_f) there is a canonical isometry of A_{f,E}-Hermitian spaces V(A_{t·y}[∞])_Q ≅ V(A_y[∞])_Q, identifying V_μ(A_{t·y}[∞]) with θ(t)^{−1}·V_μ(A_y[∞]), where θ = θ_{A_f} : T_{A_f} → Aut(V(A[∞])_Q).
proofOutline: Y is finite étale over O_E away from D_bad (Lemma 5.3.4), and its points are a T(A_f)-torsor.

items.name: Lifting depth of a special quasi-endomorphism
items.statement: With ord_𝔮 : V(A_y[p^∞]_𝔭)_Q → Z ∪ {∞} as defined on p. 500 (see the new item), for μ ∈ L_𝔭^∨/L_𝔭 and x ∈ V_μ(A_y[p^∞]_𝔭): x lifts to V_μ(A_k[p^∞]_𝔭) iff ord_𝔮(x) ≥ k. The standing hypotheses of §7.7 apply: 𝔭 is non-split in E over a good prime p, y ∈ Y(F_𝔮^alg), and k ≥ 1.

items.name: Proper intersection with the CM cycle
items.statement: If the image of Y(C) → M⋄(C) meets the support of Z⋄(m,μ)(C), then there is x ∈ D_{L⋄}^{-1}Λ with Q(x) = m. Hence, under Hypothesis 8.3.1, Z⋄(f) meets Y properly.

items.name: A lattice good at prescribed primes
items.statement: If (a, ξ') is good at every p in a finite set S, there is a maximal lattice L' ⊂ V' = (E, Tr_{F/Q}(ξ'·Nm)) that is good at every p ∈ S.

items.name: Kisin's functor on crystalline Z_p-lattices
items.statement: Let K be as in §2.1. There is a fully faithful tensor functor M from the category of Z_p-lattices Λ in crystalline Γ_K-representations to the category of Breuil–Kisin modules over O_K (with respect to ϖ), with the following properties. (2.1.1) There is a canonical isomorphism of F-isocrystals over Frac(W), M(Λ)/uM(Λ)[1/p] ≅ D_cris(Λ)=(Λ⊗_{Z_p}B_cris)^{Γ_K}. (2.1.2) With Fil^iφ*M(Λ)={x∈φ*M(Λ): φ_{M(Λ)}(x)∈E(u)^iM(Λ)}, there is a canonical isomorphism of filtered K-vector spaces (φ*M(Λ)/E(u)φ*M(Λ))[1/p] ≅ K⊗_{Frac(W)}D_cris(Λ).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18 (coverage of the paper): Theorem 2.1.1 is built on this functor, and Cor. 3.5.4 applies it to arbitrary K_q-stable crystalline lattices, whose modules need not have E-height 1. No item defines it.

items.name: Contravariant Dieudonné crystal and its Hodge filtration
items.statement: For a p-divisible group H over a p-adically complete ring R, D(H) is the contravariant Dieudonné F-crystal [BBM82]. For a nilpotent PD thickening R'→R, D(H)(R') is a finite projective R'-module, depending on the PD structure; when R' has a Frobenius lift φ there is a canonical φ: φ*D(H)(R')→D(H)(R'). On the trivial thickening there is an exact sequence 0→Lie(H)^∨→D(H)(R)→Lie(H^∨)→0 of projective R-modules, and Fil^1D(H)(R):=Lie(H)^∨ is the Hodge filtration. Examples of thickenings: R'→R'/pR' with the canonical divided powers on p, and S→O_K.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18 (coverage of the paper): A definition used in Theorem 2.1.1(1)–(3), in Prop. 2.2.1 and in the Grothendieck–Messing step of Prop. 2.5.1. No item defines it, and its variance is exactly the twist issue (E9).

items.name: Grothendieck–Messing lifting criterion for homomorphisms (Zink for p=2)
items.statement: Let R'→R be a PD thickening of p-adically complete rings with nilpotent divided powers, H1,H2 p-divisible groups over R', and a: H1_R→H2_R a homomorphism. Then a lifts to R' (necessarily uniquely) iff its crystalline realization D(a)(R'): D(H2)(R')→D(H1)(R') maps Fil^1D(H2)(R') into Fil^1D(H1)(R'). The same holds for p=2 when the groups are connected (formal), by Zink's theory of displays [Zin01]. The paper applies it to endomorphisms of G_{O_K/ϖ^{k+1}} and O_K/ϖ^{k+1}→O_K/ϖ^k.
items.locator: §2.5, proof of Proposition 2.5.1, p. 410, citing [Mes72] and [Zin01]
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18 (coverage of the paper): This is the key external deformation theorem behind Prop. 2.5.1 and Lemma 2.5.2. No item states it, and the p=2 case needs Zink's theory for connected groups.

items.name: The valuation ord_E on special quasi-endomorphisms
items.statement: In the setting of §2.5, ord_E: V(G_1)_Q→Z is the unique function such that ord_E(a·f)=ord_E(a)+ord_E(f) for a∈E^× and f∈V(G_1)_Q, and such that for an O_E-module generator f of V(G_1) (free of rank 1 by Props. 2.3.3–2.3.4), ord_E(f)=1 if E/F is unramified and ord_E(f)=ord_E(d_{E/F}) if E/F is ramified. Set ord_E(0)=∞. Every g∈V(G_1)_Q with ord_E(g)≥1 lies in V_{µ'}(G_1) for a unique µ'∈d_{E/F}^{-1}/O_E (Prop. 2.4.1(2), by counting cosets).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18 (coverage of the paper): Lemma 2.5.4 and Theorem 2.5.5 are stated in terms of ord_E. lift-depth misattributes its normalisation, and no item defines it. Route: LubinTateFormalModulesAndQuasiCanonicalLifts.

items.name: Filtered φ-module of the Lubin–Tate Tate module
items.statement: Let G be the Lubin–Tate O_E-module for π_E, base-changed to O_K along E↪K. Then T_{π_E}(G)[1/p] is a crystalline Γ_K-representation, and D_cris(T_{π_E}(G)^∨) is O_E-equivariantly isomorphic to Frac(W)⊗_{Q_p}E=⊕_ι Frac(W)_ι. Under the identification Fr*D_cris=⊕_ι Frac(W)_ι, the Frobenius is multiplication by 1⊗π_E on the Fr(ι0)-factor and the identity on the others, and Fil^1D_dR=e0·D_{ι0}.
items.locator: §2.2, proof of Proposition 2.2.1, p. 404, citing [RZ96, Lemma 1.22]
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18 (coverage of the paper): The comparison M(G)≅M rests on identifying the admissible filtered φ-module of the Lubin–Tate Tate module. This is an external input that no item states. Route: LubinTateFormalModulesAndQuasiCanonicalLifts.

items.name: Reflex norm of a torus cocharacter
items.statement: For a Q-torus A and a cocharacter µ: G_m→A with field of definition F⊂Q^alg, the reflex norm is r(A,µ)=Nm_{F/Q}∘Res_{F/Q}(µ): Res_{F/Q}G_m→Res_{F/Q}A_F→A. Its evaluations are r(A,µ)_ℓ on Q_ℓ, r(A,µ)_λ on E_λ^× and the adelic r(A,µ)(A_f): A_{f,F}^×→A(A_f). For µ0 of §3.1, r(T_E,µ0)=id and r(T,µ0): T_E→T is the quotient map.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18 (coverage of the paper): The general reflex norm is defined here and used for r(T,µ0) and r_K(T,µ0) (§3.1), for the local maps in Prop. 3.2.1 and for (3.3.1). cm-type covers only the CM-type instance.

items.name: The compact open subgroup K0⊂T(A_f)
items.statement: K0,p,so=(Z_p⊗O_E)^×/(Z_p⊗O_F)^× ⊂ T_so(Q_p)=(Q_p⊗E)^×/(Q_p⊗F)^× (3.2.1). K0,p⊂T(Q_p) is the largest compact subgroup whose image in T_so(Q_p) lies in K0,p,so. Equivalently, K0,p=Z_p^×·r(T,µ0)((Z_p⊗O_E)^×), where Z_p^×⊂Q_p^×=(T_F/T^1_F)(Q_p)=ker(T(Q_p)→T_so(Q_p)), the identification being by Nm_{F/Q}. It sits in 1→Z_p^×→K0,p→K0,p,so→1. Put K0=∏_pK0,p (compact open, but not maximal compact in general), and Y0=Y_{K0}. For p unramified in E, T extends to a torus over Z_(p) and K0,p=T(Z_p).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18 (coverage of the paper): K0 defines Y0 and the maximal-level condition of Prop. 3.2.1, and K_{L,0}=K0∩K in §5.3 (Lemma 5.3.4 uses 1→Z_p^×→K0,p→K0,p,so→1). No item defines it, and the printed definition is defective (new issues). This item uses the corrected definition. Route: ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocityPartII.

items.name: Lubin–Tate description of local reciprocity
items.statement: Let E_q/Q_p be finite, π a uniformizer, G_q the Lubin–Tate O_{E_q}-module for π, and rec_{E_q} the local Artin map. The Galois action on T_π(G_q) factors through Gal(E_q^ab/E_q) via a character χ_π: Gal(E_q^ab/E_q)→O_{E_q}^×. On inertia, χ_π∘rec_{E_q}|_{O_{E_q}^×} is u↦u^{±1}, the sign fixed by the Artin-map normalisation. In particular, I_q^ab≅O_{E_q}^× acts on T_π(G_q)[1/p] through the reciprocity isomorphism, and T_π(G_q)[1/p] is crystalline.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18 (coverage of the paper): Prop. 3.5.2, and through it §3.6, identifies the inertia action through local reciprocity with the Lubin–Tate Tate module. Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory builds local reciprocity through class formations and explicitly excludes Lubin–Tate theory, so this comparison has no owner. Route: LubinTateFormalModulesAndQuasiCanonicalLifts.

items.name: Blasius–Wintenberger: p-adic de Rham comparison respects absolute Hodge cycles
items.statement: Let A be an abelian variety over a finite extension L of Q_p, and t an absolute Hodge cycle on A (a tensor in the realizations of H^1). The p-adic comparison isomorphism B_dR⊗_{Q_p}H^1_et(A_{L̄},Q_p)≅B_dR⊗_L H^1_dR(A/L) carries the p-adic étale component of t to its de Rham component.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18 (coverage of the paper): Prop. 3.5.5(2) and the extension of t_{β,dR,Q} over Y_K rest on this theorem. It is not in the atlas; AutomorphicBundles:B1 plans absolute-Hodge statements only in general terms. Route: ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocityPartII.

items.name: Integral T-torsor of tensor-preserving de Rham trivializations
items.statement: Let D be the product of the primes at which E is ramified or K_p≠K0,p, and regard T as a torus over Z[1/D]. Choose (H,H_Z) as in Prop. 3.4.1, with tensors {t_β}⊂H_{Z_(p)}^⊗ whose stabilizer in GL(H_{Z_(p)}) is T_{Z_(p)} for p∤D, and let t_{β,dR} be their extensions over Y_K. Then the functor on Y_K[1/D]-schemes S of isomorphisms ξ: O_S⊗_Z H_Z≅H_dR|_S with ξ(1⊗t_β)=t_{β,dR} for all β is represented by a T-torsor P_T over Y_K[1/D], independent of (H,H_Z).
items.locator: §3.5, proof of Proposition 3.5.5, pp. 426–427, citing [Kis10, Cor. 1.4.3]
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18 (coverage of the paper): Away from D, the integral de Rham realization N_dR is built from this torsor. No item states it. Route: ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocityPartII.

items.name: Crystalline realization of the tautological CM representation
items.statement: Let q⊂O_E lie over p, y∈Y_K(F_q^alg), W=W(F_q^alg), π_q∈E_q a uniformizer and G_q the Lubin–Tate O_{E,q}-module. The crystalline realization H_{0,cris,y} of H0=E (T_E acting by multiplication, lattice O_E) is O_E-equivariantly ⊕_{q'|p}H_{0,cris,q'}. Here H_{0,cris,q}=D(G_q)(W) with its O_{E,q}-action, and for q'≠q, H_{0,cris,q'}=W⊗_{Z_p}O_{E,q'} with Frobenius Fr⊗1. Consequently V_{0,cris,y}=V(H_{0,cris,y},c)=⊕_{𝔭'|p}V_{0,cris,𝔭'}, where V_{0,cris,𝔭'}=V(⊕_{q'|𝔭'}H_{0,cris,q'},c) is an O_{F,𝔭'}-linear F-crystal.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18 (coverage of the paper): Prop. 3.6.1, Lemma 3.6.3 and §7 all rest on this explicit description of H_{0,cris,y} and V_{0,cris,y}. The paper asserts it ('From the proof of Proposition 3.5.2 …'), and no item states it. Route: ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocityPartII.

items.name: Newton cocharacter of an F-isocrystal
items.statement: For an F-isocrystal D over Frac(W) (W=W(F_q^alg)), Aut°_φ(D) is the Q_p-group of units of End_φ(D)_Q. The Newton cocharacter ν: 𝔻→Aut°_φ(D) (𝔻 the pro-torus over Q_p with character group Q) acts on the slope-λ summand of the Dieudonné–Manin decomposition through the character λ. D is isoclinic iff ν factors through the scalars, and an abelian variety over F_q^alg is supersingular iff the Newton cocharacter of its Dieudonné isocrystal is central (all slopes 1/2).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18 (coverage of the paper): A definition used in Prop. 3.6.2 and Lemma 3.6.3. No item defines it.

items.name: Automorphic realizations over the generic GSpin Shimura variety
items.statement: Let G → Aut(N) be an algebraic representation on a finite-dimensional Q-vector space and N_Ẑ ⊂ N_{A_f} a K-stable lattice. (i) There is a Z-local system N_B on M(C) whose fibre at [(z,g)] is N ∩ gN_Ẑ. The bundle N_{dR,M(C)} = O_{M(C)} ⊗ N_B carries a filtration Fil^• that induces on each fibre the Hodge structure of h_z. This gives a functor to variations of Z-Hodge structure. (ii) For (V, L̂) the variation (V_B, Fil^•V_dR) is polarized, with V_C^{(1,−1)} = Cz, V_C^{(−1,1)} = Cz̄ and V_C^{(0,0)} = (Cz + Cz̄)^⊥. So Fil¹V_dR is an isotropic line and Fil⁰V_dR is its annihilator. (iii) For H = C(V) (left multiplication) with H_Ẑ = C(L̂), the variation has type (−1,0),(0,−1) and is polarizable, so it is the homology of an abelian scheme A_C → M_C. This abelian scheme descends to the Kuga–Satake abelian scheme A → M, with a right C(L)-action and a compatible grading A = A⁺ × A⁻ [MP16, §3]. (iv) Using H_dR and Deligne's absolute Hodge cycles, there is a canonical tensor functor N ↦ (N_dR, Fil^•N_dR) from algebraic Q-representations of G to filtered vector bundles with integrable connection over M, descending (i). For each ℓ, Z_ℓ ⊗ N_B descends to an ℓ-adic sheaf N_ℓ over M, and H_ℓ is the ℓ-adic Tate module of A [MP16, (4.15)]. (v) Left multiplication V ↪ End_{C(V)}(H) gives embeddings V_? ↪ End_{C(L)}(H_?) for ? = B, ℓ, dR (4.1.4).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18 (coverage of the paper): Betti, de Rham and ℓ-adic realizations over the generic fibre, and the embeddings V_? ↪ End_{C(L)}(H_?), are used by every later definition of special endomorphisms. No item states them; orth-dr only extends them. Route: OrthogonalIntegralModelsAndKugaSatake.

items.name: Special divisors on the generic fibre
items.statement: For x ∈ V with Q(x) > 0, let D(x) = {z ∈ D : z ⊥ x}. For m ∈ Q_{>0} and μ ∈ L^∨/L, set Z(m,μ)(C) = ⊔_{g ∈ G(Q)\G(A_f)/K} Γ_g \ (⊔_{x ∈ μ_g + L_g, Q(x) = m} D(x)). Here Γ_g = G(Q) ∩ gKg⁻¹, L_g ⊂ V is the lattice with L̂_g = g•L̂, and μ_g = g•μ ∈ L_g^∨/L_g. Z(m,μ)(C) is the space of complex points of a disjoint union of GSpin Shimura varieties of quadratic spaces of signature (n−1,2), so it has a canonical model Z(m,μ) over Q. The natural map descends to a finite unramified morphism Z(m,μ) → M (4.1.5). Étale locally on the source this morphism is a closed immersion cut out by one equation, so it defines an effective Cartier divisor on M.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18 (coverage of the paper): The generic special divisors are defined by complex uniformization. They carry the Green functions Φ(f), and Proposition 4.5.8 and Theorem 4.8.1 identify them with the integral cycles. special-divisor covers only the integral Definition 4.5.6. Route: GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights.

items.name: ℓ-adic realizations extend over the self-dual model
items.statement: Assume L_(p) is self-dual and fix ℓ ≠ p. The functor assigns to a K_ℓ-stable Z_ℓ-lattice N_ℓ, in an algebraic representation N of G, a lisse ℓ-adic sheaf N_ℓ over M. It extends, uniquely since M_(p) is normal, to a functor to lisse ℓ-adic sheaves over M_(p), and it carries H_{Z_ℓ} to the ℓ-adic Tate module of A → M_(p). Proof: the Q_ℓ-functor comes from a canonical étale G(Q_ℓ)-torsor over M, which extends over M_(p) [MP16, (4.11), (7.9)].
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18 (coverage of the paper): The extension of ℓ-adic sheaves over M_(p) is used in Definition 4.3.1 and again in §4.5 (p. 447) to extend α_ℓ over M[1/ℓ]. Route: OrthogonalIntegralModelsAndKugaSatake.

items.name: Stacks of complement embeddings Z(Λ) and Z^pr(Λ)
items.statement: Fix p and L⋄ maximal of signature (n⋄,2), self-dual over Z_(p), with L ↪ L⋄ and Λ = L^⊥ ⊂ L⋄. Z(Λ) → M⋄_(p) is the stack with Z(Λ)(S) = {isometric embeddings Λ ↪ V(A⋄_S)} for M⋄_(p)-schemes S. It is an algebraic stack, finite and unramified over M⋄_(p) (argument of [AGHMP17, Prop. 2.7.4]). The embedding (4.4.2) gives M_(p) → Z(Λ), which identifies M with an open and closed substack of Z(Λ)_Q [MP16, Lemma 7.1]. Now let p be odd, and let Λ_dR ⊂ V⋄_dR|_{Z(Λ)} be the coherent subsheaf generated by the de Rham realization of the tautological embedding. There is a canonical open substack Z^pr(Λ) ⊂ Z(Λ), containing Z(Λ)_Q, over which Λ_dR is a local direct summand of V⋄_dR [MP16, Lemma 6.16]. Under the hypotheses of Proposition 4.4.2 it is flat and normal over Z_(p) [MP16, Cor. 6.22], and Z^pr(Λ) = Z(Λ) if p² ∤ D_L.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18 (coverage of the paper): Proposition 4.4.2, Lemmas 4.4.3–4.4.4, Theorem 4.4.5 and Proposition 4.5.8 are statements about these stacks, but no item defines them. Route: OrthogonalIntegralModelsAndKugaSatake.

items.name: Existence of auxiliary self-dual enlargements
items.statement: (a) For every prime p there is a maximal lattice L⋄ of some signature (n⋄,2), self-dual over Z_(p), with an isometric embedding L ↪ L⋄. If p is odd it can be chosen so that Λ = L^⊥ has rank at most 2, hence n⋄ ≤ n + 2. For p = 2, rank Λ must be at least the number of generators of the 2-part of L^∨/L. (b) There are maximal lattices L⋄_1, …, L⋄_r, of signatures (n⋄_i, 2), with isometric embeddings L ↪ L⋄_i and gcd(D_{L⋄_1}, …, D_{L⋄_r}) = 1.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18 (coverage of the paper): Two existence claims the construction depends on. Both are asserted as 'easily verified' or 'always possible', and the first is false at p = 2 as printed (new issue). Route: OrthogonalIntegralModelsAndKugaSatake.

items.name: Rank-one Hermitian spaces and their local invariants
items.statement: Let 𝒱 be a rank-one Hermitian space over E, negative definite at ι0 and positive definite at ι1, …, ι_{d−1}. Then 𝒬(x) = ⟨x,x⟩ is an F-quadratic form of signature ((0,2),(2,0),…,(2,0)). C(𝒱) is a quaternion algebra over F with C⁺(𝒱) ≅ E and C⁻(𝒱) = 𝒱, and left Clifford multiplication by E is the given E-structure. For any E-isomorphism 𝒱 ≅ E, the form becomes ⟨x,y⟩ = ξxȳ for a unique ξ ∈ F^×, negative at ι0 and positive at ι1, …, ι_{d−1}. The isomorphism class of 𝒱 is determined by ξ ∈ F^×/Nm_{E/F}(E^×). Conversely, every such ξ gives (E, ξNm) of signature (5.1.1). Let χ be the quadratic character of E/F and inv_v(𝒱) = χ_v(ξ). Then α ∈ F_v^× is represented by 𝒱_v if and only if χ_v(α) = inv_v(𝒱). 𝒱 is determined up to isometry by its local invariants, and ∏_v inv_v(𝒱) = 1.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18 (coverage of the paper): Rank-one Hermitian spaces are classified by ξ ∈ F^×/Nm(E^×) and by their local invariants. This defines the nearby space ^𝔭𝒱 and is used in Proposition 5.4.4 and Corollary 5.4.6. nearby-hermitian presupposes it. Route: GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights.

items.name: Local special endomorphisms at supersingular big CM points
items.statement: Let 𝔮 ⊂ O_E lie over a prime 𝔭 ⊂ O_F that is not split in E, with 𝔭 over p, and let y ∈ 𝒴(F_𝔮^alg). Then A_y is supersingular (Proposition 3.6.2), and Z_ℓ ⊗ End(A_y) → End(A_y[ℓ^∞]) is an isomorphism for every ℓ. The natural maps V(A_y[ℓ^∞]) → V_{ℓ,y} for ℓ ≠ p (5.4.3) and V(A_y[p^∞])_Q → V_{cris,y}[1/p]^{φ=1} (5.4.4) are isomorphisms, and V_{cris,y}[1/p] is generated by its φ-invariants. The T-equivariant E-action on V makes V(A_y[ℓ^∞])_Q free of rank one over Q_ℓ ⊗ E, and it carries a unique Hermitian form ⟨·,·⟩_ℓ with Q(x) = Tr_{(Q_ℓ⊗F)/Q_ℓ}⟨x,x⟩_ℓ. Hence V(A_y[∞])_Q = ∏_ℓ V(A_y[ℓ^∞])_Q is a Hermitian space over A_{f,E}.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18 (coverage of the paper): These isomorphisms and the Hermitian structure are the inputs of Propositions 5.4.4–5.4.5 and Corollary 5.4.6; they are stated between numbered results and no item covers them. Route: GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights.

items.name: Parity of Diff(α) and the nearby characterisation
items.statement: For α ∈ F^×, Diff(α) is a finite set of places of F of odd cardinality, and every v ∈ Diff(α) is non-split in E. For a finite prime 𝔭 ⊂ O_F, Diff(α) = {𝔭} if and only if α is represented by the nearby Hermitian space ^𝔭V of Definition 5.1.2.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18 (coverage of the paper): Used in Prop. 7.6.1, in the proof of Theorem 6.4.2 and throughout §7 (Diff(α) = {𝔭} ⟺ α represented by ^𝔭V). Item diff-set covers only part, and the nearby characterisation is in no item. Route: GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights.

items.name: Local Weil index and constant-term local factor
items.statement: For a finite prime 𝔭 of F: f(𝔭) = ord_𝔭(d_F D_{E/F}); γ_𝔭(V) = χ_𝔭(−1)·inv_𝔭(V)·ε_𝔭(χ,ψ_F) ∈ {±1,±i}, the local Weil index of V_𝔭 relative to ψ_{F_𝔭} ([Yan05]); they satisfy (−i)^d∏_𝔭 γ_𝔭(V) = −1 (incoherence). For φ_𝔭 ∈ S(V_𝔭) with standard section Φ_𝔭, M_𝔭(s,φ_𝔭) = N(𝔭)^{f(𝔭)/2}γ_𝔭(V)^{−1}·(L_𝔭(s+1,χ)/L_𝔭(s,χ))·W_{0,𝔭}(I,s,Φ_𝔭), with W_{0,𝔭}(I,s,Φ_𝔭) = ∫_{F_𝔭}Φ_𝔭(wn(b),s)db (6.2.3). At the archimedean places, W_{0,∞}(g_τ⃗,s,Φ_∞) = (−i)^d·Γ_R(s+1)^d/Γ_R(s+2)^d·N(v⃗)^{(1−s)/2} ([Yan05, Prop. 2.4]), so W_0(g_τ⃗,s,Φ) = −N(v⃗)^{(1−s)/2}(Λ(s,χ)/Λ(s+1,χ))M(s,φ).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18 (coverage of the paper): γ_𝔭(V) and M_𝔭 are the normalisations of every §7.1 result (W*, Prop. 7.1.8, Cor. 7.1.9, Prop. 7.8.2). No item defines them. Route: GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights.

items.name: Rankin–Selberg L-function of ξ(f)
items.statement: Let L be maximal, f ∈ H_{2−d}(ω_L) with integral principal part, and g = ξ(f) ∈ S_d(ω̄_L) its image under the Bruinier–Funke operator (4.7.3), g = Σ_μ g_μφ_μ. Define L(s,ξ(f)) = Λ(s+1,χ)∫_{SL2(Z)\H} Σ_{μ∈L^∨/L} conj(g_μ(τ))·E(τ,s,φ_μ) du dv/v^{2−d}, where E(τ,s,φ) is the restriction of E(τ⃗,s,φ) to the diagonal H ↪ H^d ([BKY12, (5.3)]). L(s,ξ(f)) is entire in s and vanishes at s = 0.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18 (coverage of the paper): It appears in Theorems 6.3.1, 6.4.2, B and (through them) A. Item diagonal-series misdescribes it. Route: GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights.

items.name: Stacky degree of the big CM cycle
items.statement: deg_C(Y) = Σ_{y∈Y(C)} 1/|Aut(y)| = |T(Q)\T(A_f)/K_{L,0}| / |T(Q) ∩ K_{L,0}|, with Y(C) the complex points of Y viewed as an E-stack. With Y^∞ = Y ×_{Spec Z} Spec C, Σ_{y∈Y^∞(C)} 1/|Aut(y)| = 2d·deg_C(Y).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18 (coverage of the paper): The normalising degree in Theorems 6.3.1, 6.4.2, 7.8.1 and Prop. 7.6.4. It is only in the result's conventions block, not in an item. Route: GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights.

items.name: Proper intersection of Y with Z(f)
items.statement: V(A_y) = 0 for every y ∈ Y(C) (Prop. 5.4.1), so the image of Y → M is disjoint in the complex fibre from the support of every Z(m,μ), hence of Z(f). Since Y is flat of relative dimension 0 over Z, Y meets Z(f) properly: Y ×_M Z(f) is 0-dimensional and supported in finitely many nonzero characteristics. Hence [Ẑ(f):Y] = deg^(Y ×_M Z(f), 0) + ½Σ_{y∈Y^∞(C)} Φ(f,y)/|Aut(y)|.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18 (coverage of the paper): It is needed to evaluate [Ẑ(f):Y] as a proper intersection, as the proof of Theorem 6.4.2 (p. 503) does. No item states it. Route: GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights.

items.name: Siegel–Weil formula for the nearby coherent Eisenstein series
items.statement: Let 𝔭 be non-split in E, ^𝔭φ ∈ S(^𝔭V̂), and E(g,s,^𝔭Φ) the coherent Eisenstein series on SL2(A_F) attached to φ^1_∞ ⊗ ^𝔭φ and the coherent space C_∞ × ^𝔭V̂ ≅ ^𝔭V ⊗_F A_F. For α ∈ F_+: E_α(g_τ⃗,0,^𝔭Φ)/√N(v⃗) = (2/Vol(T^so(Q)\T^so(A)))·∫_{T^so(Q)\T^so(A)} Σ_{x∈^𝔭V, ^𝔭Q(x)=α} ^𝔭φ(s_f^{−1}x)ds·q^α = 2·O(α,^𝔭φ)·q^α. The second equality holds because T^so(Q) acts simply transitively on {x ∈ ^𝔭V : ^𝔭Q(x) = α}.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18 (coverage of the paper): An external input ([KR94], as in [HY12, Prop. 4.4.1]) on which Prop. 7.3.2 rests. No item covers it; item fourier-orbital only mentions it in its outline. Route: GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights.

items.name: 𝔮-adic order of a special quasi-endomorphism
items.statement: ord_𝔮 : V(A_y[p^∞]_𝔭)_Q → Z ∪ {∞} is the function determined by: ord_𝔮(a·x) = ord_𝔮(a) + ord_𝔮(x) for a ∈ E_𝔮 and x ∈ V(A_y[p^∞]_𝔭); and, for x corresponding under Prop. 7.5.1 to an O_{E,𝔮}-module generator of V(G_{𝔮,y}), ord_𝔮(x) = 1 if 𝔮 is unramified over F, and ord_𝔮(x) = n(𝔭) = ord_𝔮(d_{E/F}) if 𝔮 is ramified over F.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18 (coverage of the paper): Used in Prop. 7.7.3 and Theorem 7.7.4. It is a Kuga–Satake-side definition transported by Prop. 7.5.1, distinct from ord_E on V(G_1) in §2.5 (item lift-depth). Route: LubinTateFormalModulesAndQuasiCanonicalLifts.

items.name: Lifting the Colmez class function to a larger CM field
items.statement: If E ⊂ Ẽ are CM fields, Φ is a CM type of E, and Φ̃ = {φ̃ ∈ Hom(Ẽ,Q^alg) : φ̃|_E ∈ Φ} is the lifted CM type, then [Ẽ:E]·a^0_{(E,Φ)} = a^0_{(Ẽ,Φ̃)} in CM^0.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18 (coverage of the paper): Used in the proof of Proposition 9.3.2 (p. 512); no item states it. Route: ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocityPartII.

items.name: Total reflex CM type
items.statement: Fix ι0 : E → C. Under the Γ_Q-equivariant identification Hom(E♯,Q^alg) = CM(E), let Φ♯ ⊂ Hom(E♯,Q^alg) be the set of CM types of E that contain ι0. Then Φ♯ is a CM type of the CM algebra E♯, with |Φ♯| = 2^{d−1}. (E♯,Φ♯) is the total reflex pair.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18 (coverage of the paper): Item total-reflex-algebra defines E♯ only. Φ♯ is used in Proposition 9.2.1, Corollary 9.3.3 and §9.4. Route: ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocityPartII.

items.name: Metrized Hodge, volume and standard lines on Y0
items.statement: On Y0 → Spec O_E with the abelian scheme A♯ (CM by O_{E♯}, type Φ♯): (1) Ω̂♯ = π_*Ω^{top}_{A♯/Y0} with ||s||² = |∫_{A♯_y(C)} s∧s̄|; (2) d̂et(H♯_dR) with the volume metric ||e|| = 1 for local generators e of det(H♯_B), whose dual metric on H^{2g}_dR is ||η|| = |∫η|; (3) ω̂0 = Fil^1V_{0,dR} with ||z||²_0 = |[z,z̄]_0|, where [,]_0 is the bilinear form of Q0 = Tr_{F/Q}⟨x,x⟩_0. This equals +[z,z̄]_0 at points over ι0 and −[z,z̄]_0 at points over the other real places.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18 (coverage of the paper): The three metrics that Theorem 9.4.2 compares are not stated by any item. The ω0 metric needs the amended E4 normalization. Route: ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocityPartII.

items.name: Hodge-bundle degree on Y0 as a Faltings height
items.statement: d̂eg(Ω̂♯)/deg_C(Y0) = [E:Q]·h^Falt_{(E♯,Φ♯)} = Σ_{Φ∈CM(E)} h^Falt_{(E,Φ)}. Here deg_C(Y0) counts points over the fixed embedding of E, and Y0^∞(C) has [E:Q]·deg_C(Y0) points.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18 (coverage of the paper): The bridge from arithmetic degree on the stack Y0 to the Faltings height, with the 2d-point normalization. It appears only inside the proof of Theorem 9.4.2. Route: ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocityPartII.

items.name: Metrized determinant identity for the total reflex abelian scheme
items.statement: In P̂ic(Y0): d̂et(H♯_dR) = Δ̂ + 2^{d−1}·ω̂0 − 2·Ω̂♯, where Δ̂ = (Δ,0) is the divisor of the canonical section of L (9.4.3) with zero Green function. Equivalently, that section has norm 1 at every complex point when ω0 carries ||z||²_0 = |[z,z̄]_0| (= 2^{1−d}|Tr_{H♯}(z∘z̄)|).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18 (coverage of the paper): Stated as 'easy to check'. It is the step E4 bears on, and I verified it only with the metric |[z,z̄]_0|. Route: ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocityPartII.

items.name: Arithmetic degree of the volume-metrized de Rham determinant
items.statement: d̂eg(d̂et(H♯_dR))/deg_C(Y0) = 2^d·d·log(2π). Proof: the trace-one generator of H^{2g}_dR(A♯/Y0) (g = 2^{d−1}) has |∫η| = (2π)^g at each of the 2d·deg_C(Y0) complex points.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18 (coverage of the paper): The only use of Lemma 9.4.3. Its sign fixes the −(d/2)log(2π) in Theorem A. Route: ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocityPartII.

items.name: Local Artin-conductor functional and subset class functions
items.statement: On the space of locally constant C-valued class functions on Γ_{Q_p}, μ_p is the linear functional with μ_p(χ) = log_p f_p(χ) (Artin conductor exponent) for irreducible characters χ. It is extended to locally constant f by μ_p(f) = μ_p(f^0) (Haar conjugation average); it is a distribution, not a measure. For K finite étale over Q_p and Υ ⊂ Hom(K,P), a_{(K,Υ)}(σ) = |Υ ∩ σ∘Υ|, and a_{η,η'}(σ) = 1 if σ∘η = η', 0 otherwise.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18 (coverage of the paper): A definition used by Proposition 9.4.5 and (9.4.13). The printed version needs the E23 restriction. Route: ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocityPartII.

items.name: Colmez's conductor values for embedding-pair functions
items.statement: For K a finite extension of Q_p with maximal unramified subfield K0 and uniformizer π_K, and η,η' ∈ Hom(K,P): μ_p(a_{η,η}) = e_P^{-1}·ord_{O_P}(η(𝔡_{K/Q_p})); μ_p(a_{η,η'}) = −e_P^{-1}·ord_{O_P}(η(π_K) − η'(π_K)) if η ≠ η' and η|_{K0} = η'|_{K0}; and μ_p(a_{η,η'}) = 0 otherwise.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18 (coverage of the paper): An imported key input of Proposition 9.4.5 that no item states. I spot-checked it on Q3(√3). Route: ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocityPartII.

items.name: Local total reflex pair and its averaged character
items.statement: For 𝔭 | p a prime of F, let E_𝔭 = E⊗_F F_𝔭 and d_𝔭 = [F_𝔭:Q_p]. CM(E_𝔭) is the set of Φ_𝔭 ⊂ Hom(E_𝔭,Q̄_p) with Φ_𝔭 ⊔ cΦ_𝔭 = Hom(E_𝔭,Q̄_p), and E♯_𝔭 is the étale Q_p-algebra with Hom(E♯_𝔭,Q̄_p) = CM(E_𝔭). Set Φ♯_𝔭 = {Φ_𝔭 ∋ ι0}. Then a^0_{(E♯_𝔭,Φ♯_𝔭)} = 2^{d_𝔭−2}(1 + d_𝔭^{-1}·Ind_{Γ_{F_𝔭}}^{Γ_{Q_p}} χ_𝔭), with χ_𝔭 the (possibly trivial) quadratic character of E_𝔭/F_𝔭. Also CM(E) → CM(E_𝔭) is surjective with fibres of size 2^{d−d_𝔭}.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18 (coverage of the paper): Needed for (9.4.12). Stated only as 'arguing as in Propositions 9.3.2 and 9.3.1'. Route: ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocityPartII.

items.name: Pair (𝔞, ξ') good at p
items.statement: For an ideal 𝔞 ⊂ O_E and ξ' ∈ F^× with ι0(ξ') < 0 and ι_j(ξ') > 0 (j > 0), the pair is good at p if Λ_p = (𝔞, Tr_{F/Q}(ξ'·Nm_{E/F})) ⊗ Z_p is an O_E-stable quadratic Z_p-lattice that is self-dual at every 𝔭 | p unramified in E, and satisfies Λ_𝔭^∨ ⊂ 𝔡^{-1}_{E_q/F_𝔭}Λ_𝔭 at every 𝔭 | p ramified in E. Sufficient condition used: 𝔭 ∤ ξ'·Nm_{E/F}(𝔞)·𝔡_{F/Q} for all 𝔭 | p.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18 (coverage of the paper): A definition used by Lemma 9.5.3 and Proposition 9.5.2. Item good-prime is the different Definition 5.3.3. Route: GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights.

items.name: Norm map from the class group of E to the narrow class group of F
items.statement: For E/F a CM quadratic extension, Nm : Cl(E) → Cl^+(F) is surjective iff E/F is ramified at some finite prime. If E/F is unramified at all finite primes, χ_{E/F} factors through Cl^+(F) and its kernel is exactly the image of Nm.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18 (coverage of the paper): A class-field-theory input to Proposition 9.5.2 that no item states. Tau Ceti has NarrowClassGroup (TauCeti/NumberTheory/NumberField/NarrowClassGroup/Basic.lean:83 at f790474) but not this theorem. Route: ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocityPartII.

items.name: Enlargement self-dual at a given prime with binary positive complement
items.statement: Let d ≥ 2, L ⊂ V = (E, Tr_{F/Q}(ξNm)) be maximal, and p a prime. There is a quadratic space V⋄ ⊃ V of signature (2d,2) with a maximal lattice L⋄ ⊃ L such that L⋄ ⊗ Z_(p) is self-dual. Then Λ = L^⊥ ⊂ L⋄ is a positive definite binary Z-lattice.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18 (coverage of the paper): Asserted as an 'easy exercise'. It is a genuine step in the proof of Theorem A. Route: GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights.

items.name: Infinitely many admissible primes avoid a binary positive definite form
items.statement: Let Λ be a positive definite binary Z-lattice, K = Q(√−disc Λ), and Λ_Q ≅ (K, c·Nm_{K/Q}) with c ∈ Q_{>0}. Every prime p inert in K with ord_p(c) even is not represented by Λ_Q, and there are infinitely many such primes (Chebotarev). If L⋄ ⊃ Λ is indefinite of rank ≥ 5 (here 2d+2 ≥ 6), all but finitely many of these primes are represented by L⋄ ⊂ L⋄∨. They form an infinite set S of square-free positive elements of D_{L⋄}^{-1}Z, as Theorem 9.5.6 requires.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18 (coverage of the paper): The printed claim is false (new issue). The corrected claim is what feeds Theorem 9.5.6. Route: GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights.

items.name: Averaged Colmez formula for imaginary quadratic fields (Chowla–Selberg)
items.statement: For E imaginary quadratic (d = 1, F = Q) and either CM type Φ: h^Falt_{(E,Φ)} = −½·L'(0,χ_E)/L(0,χ_E) − ¼·log|D_E| − ½·log(2π), in the normalization of Definition 9.1.4. This is Colmez's conjecture for E, the Chowla–Selberg formula ([Col93] with [Obu13] for abelian E).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18 (coverage of the paper): The §9 proof needs d ≥ 2 (new gap issue). The case d = 1 is covered only by the literature cited in §1.1. Route: ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocityPartII.

routes.reason: Height-one modules, all-prime classification, integral comparisons and generic crystalline obstruction theory are already within R07. Import them rather than expanding the pending tensor-specific Part II merely for ordinary BK theory.
The paper is a source for CM types/reflex norms; these definitions already have the generic CM owner. The total-reflex height construction is the separate CM Part II extension.

Generic finite étale torus canonical models and the reciprocity condition are V4; the integral maximal-level model and CM Hodge lattices are additional CM-specific work, not another generic Shimura canonical-model roadmap.

The existing canonical principal bundle/representation-valued realization owner supplies Betti, étale and de Rham descent, including absolute Hodge tensors. Do not duplicate this in the CM or orthogonal applications.

Generic hermitian line degree, Green-divisor formalism, stack projection/normalization interfaces and Faltings metric stay with Arakelov. The CM average and orthogonal Green evaluation are consumers, not private definitions of degree.

Finite discriminant Weil modules, adelic measure/Weil conventions and generic theta/Siegel–Weil machinery stay with MetaplecticAutomorphicForms. The specific incoherent Hilbert coefficients are a GSpin big-CM application importing these APIs.
Harmonic Maass forms, ξ, weakly holomorphic kernel and cusp-form surjectivity belong to QM.3. The paper adds a representation/conjugation normalization test for its GSpin lift.

routes.title: Finite flat group schemes and integral p-adic Hodge theory, Part II: Lubin–Tate formal modules and quasi-canonical lifts
routes.reason: Reuse the reviewed candidate ID from PAPER-BURUNGALE-KOBAYASHI-OTA-21. Its general finite-Qp formal-module foundation is exactly the common supplier; AGHMP adds the conjugate-semilinear, denominator and wild lifting-depth branch, not a second LT theory.
routes.brief: Augment LubinTateFormalModulesAndQuasiCanonicalLifts, preserving the existing Lubin–Tate reciprocity, Honda and quasi-canonical-lift obligations. Import finite flat groups and integral p-adic Hodge theory (FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.1, R07.2, R07.4, R07.6), Mathlib FormalGroup, and the existing Class field theory Artin map, never a rival reciprocity map. For arbitrary finite E/Qp construct the OE-action, LT group and explicit rank-one BK realization. For quadratic E/F construct conjugate-semilinear special endomorphisms, Hermitian composition, denominator torsors V_mu and the strict ramified different cutoff r(mu)≤v_E(d_E/F)−1. Prove AGHMP18 Theorem2.5.5: over the kth local thickening a nonzero residue special quasi-endomorphism lifts iff ord_E(f)≥k, with generator depth1 unramified and v_E(different) ramified; set ord_E(0)=∞. Prove the all-prime obstruction line and twisted OE-linearity, not just the tame/odd case. Correct the source's thickening indices and confirm Tate variance against Kisin/Kim before closing G1. Export integral and rational comparison maps to the GSpin consumer without importing that consumer. Tests must include p=2, the strict boundary r=n, zero, multiplication by a uniformizer, and an odd ramified extension with no nonzero denominator coset.

routes.title: Complex Shimura varieties and canonical models, Part II: orthogonal integral models, Kuga–Satake and special divisors
routes.reason: Reuse OrthogonalIntegralModelsAndKugaSatake from PAPER-CHARLES-16 and its all-prime extension in PAPER-SHANKAR-SHANKAR-TANG-ETAL-22, also consumed by Li–Zhang and Maulik–Shankar–Tang. This paper supplies its foundational §4 source, not another orthogonal model owner.
routes.brief: Augment the existing OrthogonalIntegralModelsAndKugaSatake proposal with AGHMP18 §4 and the total-reflex Clifford embedding of5.2. Import Complex Shimura varieties and canonical models (ShimuraVarieties V4–V6), Shimura data (ShimuraData), the pending general integral Hodge-type models (ShimuraVarietiesHondaTatePartII), canonical realizations (AutomorphicBundles B1–B2), Abelian schemes and arithmetic moduli (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A4–A5), finite flat groups and integral p-adic Hodge theory (R07.2, R07.4, R07.6), and Mathlib CliffordAlgebra/TauCeti.IntegralLattice. For maximal L of signature(n,2), construct GSpin, full-Clifford KS of dimension2^(n+1), its realizations, smooth self-dual models including2, and auxiliary-independent flat normal integral models. Prove Theorem4.4.6 with the verified dimension restrictions, the extended Hodge line, finite enlargement maps and Serre tensor comparison. Construct realization-defined special endomorphisms and denominator cosets, their positive norm on connected bases, Z(m,mu), complement pullbacks and4.5.8 Cartier/flatness with n≥3 and self-dual-at2 hypotheses where needed. Prove principal deformation equations and rigidity separately from Cartier non-zero-divisor assertions. No height or theta lift is owned here. Tests: norm-one Spin is not GSpin, connected versus disconnected scalar norm, m=0, nontrivial discriminant gluing, dyadic self-dual case and change of auxiliary enlargement. G2 and the external KMP16 appendix-erratum scope must be settled before closure.

routes.title: Gross–Zagier formulas and arithmetic heights, Part II: heights of GSpin special divisors and exceptional reductions
routes.reason: Reuse GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights from the existing SST22/Li–Zhang22/Maulik–Shankar–Tang22 proposals. Ordinary Borcherds Green functions and big-CM arithmetic intersections belong here; do not duplicate the distinct HigherGreenFunctionCMValues proposal or curve-level GZ.6–7.
routes.brief: Add the AGHMP18 big-CM branch to GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights without replacing its existing exceptional-reduction goals. Import OrthogonalIntegralModelsAndKugaSatake for the integral stack, KS and special divisors; LubinTateFormalModulesAndQuasiCanonicalLifts for exact special-endomorphism lift depth; CM types and torus realizations from ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocity, ShimuraVarieties V4 and AutomorphicBundles B1–B2; ArakelovGeometryAndAbelianHeights R35.1–2 for degree/metric; MetaplecticAutomorphicForms MP.4–6, QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms QM.3 and AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors AL.1 for analytic inputs. Construct big CM Y, good primes, nearby Hermitian lines, denominator-truncated Schwartz functions, normalized Whittaker integrals, weighted orbital integrals, Z_F(alpha,mu) and the regularized Green arithmetic divisor. Prove Theorem7.7.4's local length ell, Theorem7.8.1 deg Z_F/deg_C Y=−a_F/Λ(0), and Theorem6.4.2: for d>1 and f∈H_(2−d)(omega_L) with integral principal part, [Zhat(f):Y]/deg_C Y≈_L−L'(0,xi f)/Λ(0)+a(0,0)c_f^+(0,0)/Λ(0). The ambiguity is exactly rational logs at D_bad,L. Prove the integral Borcherds metric identity with log(4πe^γ), positive-complement contraction, proper-support criterion and8.3.4 with nonzero constant term. Add Bruinier's prescribed-negative-support theorem9.5.6. Keep finite L and completed Λ separate, E-stack degree versus Z-complex multiplicity2d, all stabilizers and dyadic/wild cases. Resolve the raw/normalized Whittaker signs and all G3 input hypotheses before activating the formulas. Export the Hodge height and good-prime vertical-error vanishing to the CM height consumer, not the averaged Colmez identity itself.

routes.brief: Augment ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocityPartII with AGHMP18's independent proof of the averaged Colmez formula, preserving the Yuan–Zhang corrected quaternionic branch and quantitative/orbit branches. For every maximal-order CM field E/F, [F:Q]=d, prove 2^(-d)Σ_all types h_Falt(E,Phi)=−(1/2)L_f'(0,chi)/L_f(0,chi)−(1/4)log(D_E/D_F)−(d/2)log(2π) using AGHMP's unscaled squared volume metric; prove the adapter h_YZ=h_AGHMP+d log(2π)/2. Import generic CM types/reflex norms (ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocity CM.0/CM.2), torus canonical models (ShimuraVarieties V4), canonical realization tensors (AutomorphicBundles B1–B2), integral BK comparisons (FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.4), Arakelov geometry (R35.1–2), generic Artin/Hecke conductors (AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors AL.1), and GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights for the big-CM Hodge height. Construct integral maximal-level CM realizations, total reflex algebra/type, its polarized abelian scheme, CM class functions and determinant section. Prove Colmez's height linearity as an input, the averaged character identities, local partition-resultant/conductor lengths with corrected signs, and the local/global discriminant degree. Repair the positive ω0 metric, arbitrary-generator trace lemma and false full-lattice scaling assertion before proving9.4.2/9.5.1. Vary auxiliary lattices to remove each bad-prime log coefficient, using good-prime Borcherds and prescribed negative support. Provide the d=1 classical input. The individual Colmez conjecture is not a proved endpoint or assumption. Tests include d=1, product reflex algebra, the ramified quadratic length1 (not−1), level-invariant normalized degrees and nonzero constant term. G4–G6 are hard activation gates, not silently assumed lemmas.

review.reason: Over ι0 the Betti realization of V0 is V0 itself, with Q0 = Tr_{F/Q}(uū) positive definite, so −[z,z̄]_0 < 0 there. Let B be the indefinite quaternion algebra over Q of discriminant 15, V = B⁰ (trace zero) with Q = Nrd, of signature (1,2), and L = O_B ∩ B⁰ for a maximal order O_B. At 3 and 5, V is anisotropic and L is the unique maximal lattice; at 2 its discriminant is 2; so L is maximal with D_L = 2·3²·5² = 450. Since dim V = 3, G = C⁺(V)^× and K_ℓ = C⁺(L_ℓ)^×. For ℓ = 3, 5, take the basis e1 = u, e2 = Π, e3 = uΠ of L_ℓ (u² = ε a non-square unit, Π² = ℓ). With α = e1e2 and β = e1e3, C⁺(L_ℓ) = Z_ℓ⟨1, α, β, αβ⟩ and Nrd(a + bα + cβ + dαβ) = a² + εℓb² − ε²ℓc² − ε³ℓ²d². Hence ν(K_ℓ) = (Z_ℓ^×)². So π_0(M(C)) = Q^×_{>0}\A_f^×/ν(K) ≅ (Z/2)², and M, which is proper because V is anisotropic, has four geometric components with constant field Q(√−3, √5). At p = 7 (odd, 7² ∤ 450, L_(7) self-dual), M_(7) is smooth and proper over Z_(7). Its ring of constants O_{Q(√−3,√5)} ⊗ Z_(7) is étale of degree 4, so by Stein factorization M_{F̄_7} has four connected components and (3) fails. sourceIssues.locator: §2.3, Proposition 2.3.1, p. 405 (journal image checked; identical in Colmez_v3.5.pdf)
sourceIssues.printed: 'Given a p-adically complete O_E-algebra R … PROPOSITION 2.3.1. (1) The subspace V(G_R) ⊂ End(G_R) is O_E-stable. If it is non-zero, then it is a finite free O_E-module of rank 1. (2) For any x1, x2 ∈ V(G_R), there exists a unique ⟨x1,x2⟩ ∈ O_E such that x1∘x2 = [⟨x1,x2⟩] ∈ End_{O_E}(G_R).'
sourceIssues.correction: Add the hypothesis that Spec R is connected (R≠0). Then End_{O_E}(G_R)=O_E, and (1)–(3) hold.
sourceIssues.reason: Counterexample: take R=F_p^alg×F_p^alg, a p-adically complete O_E-algebra. Then G_R=G_{F_p^alg}⊔G_{F_p^alg}, so V(G_R)=V(G_1)×V(G_1)≅O_E², free of rank 2 by Props. 2.3.3–2.3.4, and End_{O_E}(G_R)=O_E×O_E, so x1∘x2 need not be a scalar of O_E. For connected R, O_E-linear endomorphisms reduce injectively (rigidity) to R/p, where [π_E](X)=X^q forces coefficients c with c^q=c, which are constant; hence End_{O_E}(G_R)=O_E. The paper applies the proposition only to the local rings O_K/ϖ^k and F_p^alg, so nothing downstream is affected.

sourceIssues.printed: 'Now, W[u]/(u^k) → O_K/ϖ^k is a divided power thickening, its kernel being the ideal (p, u^{k−1}), and f̃_{k+1}, by virtue of being characterized by its φ_k-invariance, is the evaluation of the crystalline realization of f on this thickening.'
