sourceIssues.locator: §2.5, proof of Lemma 2.5.3, p. 413 (and hence Theorem 2.5.5, p. 414) (journal image checked; identical in Colmez_v3.5.pdf)
sourceIssues.printed: 'Suppose first that k < e … and suppose that ob_{k+2}(a·f) = 0. We then claim that ob_{k+1}(f) = 0. Indeed, this follows easily from assertion (2) of Lemma 2.5.2 … This shows the lemma when k < e. Now suppose that k ≥ e. Then the map O_K → O_K/ϖ^k is a divided power thickening.' Lemma 2.5.2(2): 'Suppose that k < e and that f ∈ V_µ(G_k).'
sourceIssues.correction: Treat k=e−1 separately. One option is to extend Lemma 2.5.2(2) to k=e, using the PD thickening W[u]/(u^{e+1})→O_K/ϖ^e (kernel (p,u^e)) in place of M_{e+1}, which the text defines only for k≤e. Alternatively, for p odd, apply the second argument, since ϖ^{e−1}O_K carries divided powers when e(p−2)≥p−1.
sourceIssues.reason: For k=e−1, the first case needs Lemma 2.5.2(2) for a·f∈V_{aµ}(G_{k+1}) at level k+1=e, but 2.5.2(2) assumes k<e, and V_{k+1}=V(M_{e+1},τ) is not defined (M_k is defined only for k≤e). The second case needs O_K→O_K/ϖ^{e−1} to be a PD thickening. That holds iff e−1≥e/(p−1), which fails for p=2. So for p=2 and E/Q_2 ramified (e≥2), the step k=e−1 of the induction behind Theorem 2.5.5 is not covered by any argument in the text. Theorem 2.5.5 feeds Prop. 7.7.3 (p. 501) at every good prime, and Definition 5.3.3 allows p=2. The statement is expected to hold, and the extension of 2.5.2(2) looks routine, so this is recorded as a gap, not an error.

sourceIssues.locator: §3.2, pp. 416–417 (journal images checked; identical in Colmez_v3.5.pdf)
sourceIssues.printed: p. 416: 'We will now choose a particular maximal compact K0 ⊂ T(A_f).' p. 417: 'Now define K0,p ⊂ T(Q_p) to be the largest subgroup mapping to K0,p,so ⊂ T_so(Q_p), and to ⊕_{𝔭|p} Z_p^×/Nm(O_{F_𝔭}^×) under (3.2.2). It sits in a short exact sequence 1 → Z_p^× → K0,p → K0,p,so → 1.'
sourceIssues.correction: K0,p := the largest compact subgroup of T(Q_p) whose image in T_so(Q_p) lies in K0,p,so. This equals Z_p^×·r(T,µ0)((Z_p⊗O_E)^×), with Z_p^×⊂Q_p^×=(T_F/T^1_F)(Q_p); the cohomological condition then holds automatically. Read 'maximal compact' as 'compact open'.
sourceIssues.reason: The printed K0,p is not compact. The image of p∈Q_p^×⊂(Q_p⊗F)^×⊂T_E(Q_p) in T(Q_p) maps to 1 in T_so (p/p̄=1) and to 0 in the cokernel of (3.2.2), since it comes from T_E(Q_p). Yet Nm: T→G_m sends it to p^{2d}, so its powers are unbounded. It is also a non-unit (p^d) element of ker(T(Q_p)→T_so(Q_p))=Q_p^×, contradicting 1→Z_p^×→K0,p→K0,p,so→1. The corrected group satisfies that sequence, contains r(T,µ0)_q(O_{E,q}^×) (proof of Prop. 3.2.1), equals T(Z_p) for p unramified in E (proof of Prop. 3.5.5), and is what Lemma 5.3.4 uses. It is not maximal compact in general. Example: d=2, p inert in F, 𝔭 ramified in E, t=y·[π_E] with y↔p^{-1}∈Q_p^×=(T_F/T^1_F)(Q_p). Then t²=[π_E²/p]∈K0,p, but θ(t)=π_E/π̄_E∉K0,p,so, so ⟨K0,p,t⟩ is a larger compact subgroup.

sourceIssues.printed: Statement: 'Given a prime q ⊂ O_E, we can also canonically associate with the pair an F-crystal N_cris over Y_{K,F_q}.' sourceIssues.reason: The statement asserts N_cris for every prime q, but the proof builds it only when Y_{K,q} is étale. sourceIssues.locator: Proposition 4.4.1(4), p. 441, and its proof, p. 442; its only use is the proof of Proposition 5.3.1, p. 459
sourceIssues.printed: (4) M_(p) has the following extension property: if E/Q_p is a finite extension, and t ∈ M(E) is a point such that A_t has potentially good reduction over O_E, then the map t : Spec(E) → M extends to a map Spec(O_E) → M_(p). … Assertion (4) is immediate from the finiteness (hence properness) of the map M_(p) → X_{2^{n+2},m,Z(p)}. — and on p. 459: 'Proof. This follows from Proposition 3.6.2 and assertion (4) of Proposition 4.4.1.'
sourceIssues.correction: Require that A_t has good reduction over O_E. Then the valuative criterion for the finite, hence proper and representable, map M_(p) → X gives the extension. With only potentially good reduction, t extends over O_{E'} for a finite extension E'/E. In the proof of Proposition 5.3.1, cite Proposition 3.4.1 (A_H extends to an abelian scheme over 𝒴_K) in place of Proposition 3.6.2, which is a supersingularity criterion.
sourceIssues.reason: An extension Spec O_E → M_(p) pulls A back to an abelian scheme over O_E with generic fibre A_t, so A_t must have good reduction. Every object of M has the automorphism −1: it lies in G(Q) ∩ K since Z^× ⊂ C(L̂)^×, and it acts on A as [−1]. Take t with A_t of good reduction, for example the generic point of an O_E-point of M_(p). Twisting t through this automorphism by a ramified quadratic character χ of E gives t^χ ∈ M(E) with A_{t^χ} = A_t ⊗ χ. By Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich, A_t ⊗ χ has potentially good but not good reduction, since inertia acts on T_ℓ through χ. So t^χ does not extend. The only application concerns the abelian schemes A_H of §3, which have good reduction over 𝒴 (Proposition 3.4.1), so no later result is affected. The extraction's gap G2 and a unit test of orth-normalization note the point but record no sourceIssue. The authors' version has the same text.

sourceIssues.printed: We will choose it so that Λ = L^⊥ ⊂ L⋄ has rank at most 2. This is not strictly necessary, but it will make some proofs shorter. Moreover, it is always possible to make such a choice, as can be easily verified using the classification of quadratic forms over Q.

At p = 2, rank Λ must be at least the number of generators of the 2-part of L^∨/L, which can be 3. The choice is used only for odd p: Proposition 4.4.2, the bound n⋄ ≤ n + 2 after Lemma 4.4.4, Theorem 4.4.5 and Proposition 4.5.8.
sourceIssues.reason: Here p is any fixed prime (p. 441). If L⋄ is self-dual at p, then L = L⋄ ∩ V because L is maximal, and Z_p ⊗ L^∨/L ≅ Z_p ⊗ Λ^∨/Λ (p. 448), so rank Λ is at least the minimal number of generators of the p-part of L^∨/L. For L = A_1 ⊕ A_1 ⊕ A_1 ⊕ U ⊕ U, of signature (5,2), L^∨/L = (Z/2)³ with q(x) = (x1² + x2² + x3²)/4 mod 1. This form is anisotropic (values 1/4, 1/2, 3/4), so L is maximal. sourceIssues.locator: Proof of Theorem 9.5.5, p. 526 (image checked)
sourceIssues.printed: Any rational prime not split in the discriminant field of Λ will fail to be represented by Λ_Q.
sourceIssues.correction: Write Λ_Q ≅ (K, c·Nm_{K/Q}) with K = Q(√−disc Λ), c ∈ Q_{>0}. Every prime p inert in K with ord_p(c) even is not represented, and there are infinitely many (Chebotarev). All but finitely many of them are represented by L⋄ (indefinite, rank 2d+2 ≥ 6), so they form an admissible infinite S for Theorem 9.5.6.
sourceIssues.reason: Counterexamples: Λ = Z² with x²+y² has K = Q(i), and the ramified prime 2 = 1+1 is represented. Λ with 3x²+3y² has 3 inert in Q(i) and 3 = Q(1,0) represented. For p inert and ord_p(c) even, p/c has odd valuation and is not a local norm from the unramified K_p. The proof needs only an infinite S. It also silently needs S ⊂ Q(L⋄∨), which holds as stated.

summaryBefore: The paper proves the averaged Colmez formula for maximal-order CM abelian varieties by evaluating arithmetic intersections of special divisors with a big CM cycle on GSpin integral models, including ramified and dyadic local deformation calculations. The finite-L normalization includes −d log(2π)/2. This extraction routes the local lifting package to the existing Lubin–Tate proposal, integral orthogonal geometry to the existing Kuga–Satake proposal, the big-CM intersection package to the existing GSpin divisor-height proposal, and total-reflex/height comparison to the existing CM Part II. Several printed local-length, metric, lattice and Whittaker formulas require correction or further source-level verification; no claim of disproof of the averaged Colmez theorem is made.
